notes.about: Setting data for the No Haven on Earth Atlas (mech-lineage-atlas.html). The page reads this file; other tools can too.
notes.GENS: The shared generation scale, Gen 0 to Gen 9. Every tab with eras uses these labels; a tree whose own cols differ (Fleets & Carriers splits Gen 6, Persons of Interest joins Gen 1–2 and 3–4) keeps its own column indexes.
notes.DATA: One tree per key. Node fields: id; f family; c column (era index into cols, or COLS when the tree has none); r row; m maker or type code (a GROUPS key); d designation or year; n name; s spec; t tagline; x text; p parents as [id, relation], where relation is a key of the tree's rel; fr built on; mx machines; pw power; wp weapons; dc doctrine; z line-end note.
notes.ART: node id → art file stem: art/<stem>-scene.jpg, art/<stem>-tech.jpg, thumb/<stem>-scene.jpg
notes.VART: Named variant (a variant name in ACES fr) → art file stem, same files as ART; shown with that version on its base frame's detail sheet and on ace cards
notes.PLATES: Tree key → a standalone scene shown beside that tree's intro: f art stem (art/<f>.jpg), h title, c caption, go entries it links to
notes.SCENES: Key art: id → one standalone scene shown on that entry. A tree or conflict id shows on its detail sheet, an ace id on the ace card, UNEL, or the k of a POWERS or SPACE card, on that Successors card, a TIMELINE lane's group code on that lane, and "headline" in the page header. f art stem (art/<f>.jpg), h title, c caption, t 1 for a tall (portrait) image, which the card shows whole
notes.BLOC: Map blocs, then the war map's successor powers: code → [name, colour variable, article]. PB, PM and EUX are the Pact's halves after the Sealed Session, used on the 2186 map only
notes.OVR: Per-era overrides by Natural Earth 110m country name. l: m member, a backed or partner state, n non-aligned (before the League); w: fighting in that era
notes.FUTURE: The war map (Gen 5). FUTURE members, FUTURE_SPHERE within a power's sphere, FUTURE_FRONT contested frontline held by influence (key "" means no single power), FUTURE_FIGHTING members whose own territory is a front line. The Gen 6–9 Earth map reuses FUTURE and FUTURE_SPHERE, shows FUTURE_FRONT as influence without control, keeps CANADA_SPLIT and drops the fighting hatch; FUTURE_OVR changes it per generation
notes.FUTURE_OVR: Post-war Earth map overrides by Natural Earth country name, one object per generation from Gen 6 (index = Gen − 6): {b bloc, l m member | s sphere | c influence}
notes.LOC: Conflict id → [lon, lat, place] on the map's Earth view, in any generation
notes.MINOR: Map-only smaller incidents. at: [lon, lat, place]; cty: countries hatched as fighting in that era (fighting types only)
notes.SOLAR: The map's inner-system view, every generation. bodies: key → {n name, r orbit radius and a angle in degrees from the sun, or of/dx/dy for a moon, or x/y fixed; s drawn radius}; at: entry id → [body key, place]. earth means Earth orbit and the lanes near it: events on Earth's surface use LOC, and on the Moon or Mars SITES as well.
notes.MAPNOTE: The map's note per generation, Gen 0–9: [heading, text]
notes.SITES: Places on the map's Moon and Mars views: view (moon, mars) → conflict id → list of sites. A site is [lon, lat, place] in degrees, east positive (selenographic or areocentric), or on Mars ["phobos" | "deimos", place], pinned in the band above the map. An entry with several sites shows the same numbered pin at each.
notes.MOON: The Moon view's drawing. panels: three disks, k near | pole | far; c centre [lon, lat] (orthographic), or pole with span: an azimuthal-equidistant view of the south pole out to span degrees, which takes every site that close to the pole; r radius; x, y centre. maria are filled shapes and rings outlines, each a [lon, lat] list or {c: [lon, lat, radius in degrees]} (dash 1: dashed). labels: [lon, lat, text, kind (sea, crater), priority: 1 always, 2 on wide screens or zoomed in]. towns: settlements [lon, lat, name, first Gen, last Gen].
notes.MARS: The Mars view's drawing, equirectangular, W × H. lowlands, uplands, caps and rise (Tharsis) are shapes as in MOON; volcanoes and craters [lon, lat, radius in degrees]; canyons [lon, lat] polylines; labels as in MOON (kinds region, feat); towns as in MOON, with an optional 6th field: region (an area name, no marker) or left (label on the left); lines {n name, k loc | wall, from and to Gen, pts}; moons: the bodies in the band above the map.
notes.people: DATA.people is the Persons of Interest tree: s holds life dates; p links are family (D parent, L further back) or X (mentor, rival, ally); ln may name aces as well as entries. Heroes' stories come from the First Martian Crisis players; the atlas wins any conflict.
notes.mysteries: DATA.mysteries is the Mysteries tab: open plot hooks per generation of both settings. Kinds are the M* GROUPS codes; fx says which faction views show each hook; p joins hooks that may be the same mystery.
notes.FACTION_VIEWS: Faction views chosen on the landing screen. factions: k key; n name in 2327; h Haven-era name (Earth powers); card the Successors card (POWERS b code, SPACE name or UNEL); lanes Timeline lanes the faction owns; tl lanes shown on the Factions tab; aces ace factions; bands Persons of Interest bands. makers: GROUPS code → factions, for entries tagged by maker; entries tagged by type carry their own fx list. own: codes that count for a person's faction besides their band.
notes.POWERS: The five Earth powers of No Peace Past Luna (2327). ax: five values from −2 to 2 along AXES, left pole to right; null is undecided (TBD); k: the origin entry whose key art (SCENES) shows on the card; from: entries in this atlas the power starts from (a tree entry id, or an ace id)
notes.SPACE: Colonial and outer-system factions. b: the Earth bloc each descends from (colour only); k as in POWERS; from: entries in this atlas the faction starts from (a tree entry id, or an ace id)
notes.TIMELINE: Faction lanes. ev: [era column, year label, text, entry id to open (optional)]
notes.ACE_FACTIONS: Aces tab factions: [key, name, colour code]
notes.ACE_ERAS: Aces tab era blurbs: [Gen number, an index into GENS, text]
notes.ACES: Aces tab. n name; r rank; cs callsign; g ACE_FACTIONS key; c Gen number (an index into GENS); y years active; sv service; fr frames flown, signature first, as [base frame id, S standard | V variant | C custom, variant designation and name (empty when flown as built), note or differences]; k record; x text; z where they are now; cf conflicts; ln other entries
notes.ORGMAP: Map pins for non-government organisations (orgs tree id → place). at: [lon, lat, place] sites on the Earth view; moon, mars: sites as in SITES, with an optional 4th field, the last Gen that site is used; sys: [SOLAR body key, place] a pin on the inner-system view; sky: the place in words, and an organisation with no other place (no known address) is listed under the Earth view; to: the last Gen it exists in. Without to, an organisation runs from its own column to Gen 9 if it has a moon, mars or sys place or starts after the war, otherwise to the war (Gen 5). Where the atlas names no city, the pin sits in its home country and says so.
notes.CHRONO: Front-page timeline: curated beats in order. y date label ('c.' = estimated), s sort key, e Gen number, 0–9 (the page takes the eras from the conflicts cols, which are GENS; 9 = 2327), k kind (W war, T machines, P politics, O off-world, S secrets), f TIMELINE lane indices whose story it belongs to, t title, x one line, id entry to open

KHM: Eurasian Pact (Beijing) → China and the Celestial Prosperity Syndicate
BOR: Canada, between the blocs → split by the war
EAS: From the Pact split → Eurasian Ascendancy
USA: US Navy → United States of the Americas
UNL: United Nations of Earth and Luna
EXP: Sold to anyone who can pay
LUN: Shackleton Works · built for the UN
BKG: Not a conflict, but it mattered
MLO: People, ships and things that vanished
MFR: Places that answer to no one
MMC: Frames and software that won't behave

GEN_NOTES: Two centuries of warming have already badly damaged the planet that the United States, the Continental Union and the Eurasian Pact share, and in 2159 the resource states sign the Non-Aligned Declaration.
The first mech battles: Iron Gate in the Zagros, the Pamir clash in the Wakhan Corridor, the Caspian Crisis over Azerbaijan, and an undeclared US–Union war over the Union's North African partners.
The Zarqa Campaign sets every bloc's doctrine, convoy raids drive the blocs out of Africa and Arabia, and in 2177 the African states found the Pan-African League.
The two Western blocs fight each other at Svalbard, India joins the Pact, the League's civil war turns into three proxy wars in the Great Sand Sea, and Ascension's lunar half declares a republic.
Super robots become the blocs' deterrent and Colony One is founded on Mars, while underneath the alliances that will fight the coming war start to take shape.
The Third World War, fought across Earth and for the first time in orbit, which ends when Luna's fleets force a peace under the UN's flag.

About a hundred and twenty years in which the UNEL keeps the peace on Earth and Luna while Mars, the Belt and the outer settlements grow into factions of their own. It is the longest age in the atlas and the least explored, and most of its stories are still to be told.
Eight months in which every Earth power parks a battlegroup over Mars and Colony One turns on the United States, though the fighting stays beyond Luna.
After Mars the partisan war burns on, the United States builds the Constitutionalists to replace Colony One, and the UNEL's two wings stop pretending to agree.
The projected setting of No Peace Past Luna, in which every power's grip on space is tested at once.

frames.c: Mechanics check a wing hinge on an HX-4 Merlin in a coastal hangar at sunset, its tethered LR-1 rifle cradled beside it and still cabled to the capacitor pack. Only a dozen Merlins were built, and they proved a frame could fold into flight.

vehicles.c: An M9 Teamster stands watch at an alpine road tunnel in a midnight snowstorm while a truck and two tracked supply carriers file past its knees. More Teamsters serve than any other US frame, and the vehicles still do the hauling.

supers.c: A CX-1 Concord rides a heavy-lift pontoon through a canal lock in predawn rain, chained down with its weapons stowed. The 17 m escort frame on the dock reaches less than halfway up it. A dozen exist, all of them built partly for show.

fleets.c: An AWX-1 Marlinspike drifts on a safety tether above the lunar far side, solar wings out, beside the warship whose catapult it was built for. It has no legs, and its first pilots are still working out how to fight in it. By 2327 every carrier launches its descendants.

orgs.c: A house Rigger anchors to the torn truss of an abandoned station past the elevator and lifts out a greenhouse module that is still growing. Its two operators live in the doubled cab for a week at a time. The prospecting houses keep their own books, and claims like this one are what they settle by tether duel.

fb2.c: An early start at the motor pool. A Teamster pilot laces her boots on an ammunition crate while her crew chief checks her harness, and her frame's muddy ankle fills the bay behind them.

o5.c: On a Kestrel's boarding platform, an instructor catches a twisted harness strap before a new pilot puts her helmet on. The forty-minute clock starts later; the checklist starts now.

fn2.c: Under a shelter, with their two Ashvins waiting beyond, a sworn pair rehearse the same hand signals before the helmets go on. Each knows the other's small habits by now.

og_tw.c: Through an Elissa's open cab door, the pilot in the forward seat checks that the medic behind her can reach his straps and headset. Tunis designed the cab around the second seat.

fl2.h: Access is part of the machine
fl2.c: On an Albedo's boarding platform, a pilot checks her prosthetic socket before securing her boot. The transfer rail and the handholds are as much a part of the frame as the dozer blade.

fa2.c: In a pressurised airlock, two Rigger crew check each other's helmet rings before they change places. The four-armed frame waits beyond the window.

wE9.c: Behind a broken concrete pier, a medic dresses a soldier's arm while he holds the lamp himself, and the radio operator listens for an evacuation slot. Beyond the shelter a stretcher goes by in the rain.

wS8.c: A League diplomat, a Union envoy, an interpreter and the local water board meet at a schoolroom table and turn the map so that everyone can see the same disputed valve. Their escorts wait outside.

xc3.c: On a wet container quay, an inspector's lamp finds something behind the ordinary freight: one enormous mechanical joint. The cut seal is already in an evidence bag, and nobody has taken the paperwork yet.

og_khm.c: At a workshop meeting in Darkhan, a stores worker lays an empty component tray beside a contract proposal. The machinist has the floor, and the vote is coming.

fg0.c: At a roadside repair yard, the owner serves supper while her apprentice clears the last chair. One visitor keeps a sealed case by their boot. The questions can wait until after the meal.

wW11.c: In a damaged school, a teacher marks the desks that can still be used, a League engineer measures a doorway and a returned neighbour tests a mended window latch. They are deciding which room opens first.

wW5.c: Two soldiers carry a casualty across open ground towards a doorway as fresh impacts strike the wall behind them. Inside, someone is already reaching out to guide them in.

vg4.c: A Kestrel pilot is trapped behind a cracked canopy, and a rescue engineer forces a spreader into the jammed seam. The recovery truck can lift the wreck later. The pilot comes out first.

o17.c: As a security shutter comes down, a laboratory technician slides a sealed data case through the last gap to the investigator on the other side. He still expects to follow it.

wP6.c: In a flooded town, a boat operator holds a launch against a submerged bus stop while a relief worker helps a passenger across the boarding board. The wheelchair is already lashed aboard.

wO15.c: Suited and tethered, two dock workers haul a jammed cargo trolley clear of an emergency bulkhead so that the door can close on the damaged compartment beyond.

o11.c: On a station service platform at night, an agent's earpiece gives nothing but static. A rail dispatcher pulls the gate shut and points down the maintenance passage. She has to decide whether to trust him.

ft2.c: A pilot who has abandoned his disabled Tieshan crouches behind an irrigation wall as a farmer opens the orchard gate. Behind them, helicopters hold the wreck in their searchlights.

headline.c: Dawn at a dry river crossing in 2186. A sand-worn League industrial frame rests beside its supply carriers while crews and civilians get ready to move. Across the river a Kestrel waits by its battery pit, and the city behind them is burning.

fb1.c: An M4 Garrison crouches in a foothill motor pool, its M30 pointed at the ground and its pile bunker folded. From behind, the tank it grew out of is plain to see: the sloped glacis, the cupola head, the turbine louvres.

fh3.c: A Kestrel has just landed on a closed highway in the morning haze, knees still bent and dust settling. It carries its LR-3 and two missiles under each wing binder. The fans make no flame and no smoke.

xc1.c: Three Concords loom over a press stand on an airbase apron at dusk, more than twice the height of the frames parked beside them. The pilot pair stand on the chest walkway. It was meant to look like a triumph.

wS1.c: Four Garrisons ambush a tank column from a Zagros ravine in 2162. The lead frame fires a shoulder missile uphill. The tanks can't climb to where they stand.

wS7.c: At night on the Malan Bridge, the Choir kneels across the approach and holds one forearm over the crossing to catch shrapnel. Buses, handcarts and families keep moving beneath it. Its rifle stays slung.

wO1.c: Striking workers hold a pressure bulkhead aboard an orbital construction station in 2166. A four-armed AW-3 Lifter braces the structure with its upper arms and holds a rivet driver and a welding torch in its lower pair. Security waits beyond a sealed door.

c2.c: An armourer opens the stock of an LR-3 in a forward workshop to service the MHI capacitor inside. No tether runs to a power pack. Through the hangar door, a Kestrel's leg gives the rifle its scale.

q2.c: Night rain in a highway pit. An Osprey's crane arm lowers a fresh QX pack into the spine of a kneeling Kestrel, guided by crew on the catwalks. The whole swap takes about a minute and a half.

o14.c: A Pavise leads from a foggy ridge with its antenna panels open and its coilgun braced on a bipod. Two Hauberts follow it through the valley. Below, the enemy's headlights wander. You can't see the jamming, only what it does.

va22.c: Three Kafilas, turretless tank hulls packed with fuel drums, spares and shade cloth, halt at a desert rest stop at blue hour. Mechanics check tracks while a family takes on water. A Haboob stands guard far behind.

vc21.c: A Heron carries four QX packs on one sling pallet up an Afghan valley toward a forward pit, where an Osprey and a kneeling Kestrel wait.

yg22.c: A Safina, once a bucket-wheel mining crawler, rolls ahead of a sandstorm with its hangar doors open on a row of Haboobs. One frame walks down the ramp. The deck carries workshops, water treatment and a small refinery.

yh30.c: The only Rookery holds station over a cloud deck at dawn on its four ducted fans, well away from any fighting. A Harrier is secured on the service deck beside a crane and a battery pack.

sfe0.c: An armed station tug escorts a civilian tender past a construction ring in 2186. Its weapons are a rivet gun and a cutting rig bolted to its truss. A tethered worker on the hull gives the scale.

og_mhi.c: In Mitsurugi's coastal works, technicians hand-calibrate an unarmed Kizuna's fingers from a gantry. In the next bay, the capacitors that Mitsurugi sells abroad roll past on carts.

ac05.c: Gloria Abernathy defends her swap pit near Shindand during the Hari River Offensive. Her Osprey's crane arm keeps a pack steady in its socket while the other hand aims an M30 over the berm. Her crew shelter in the revetments beside a kneeling Kestrel.

QAC.c: Delegates, engineers and repair crews argue around a plain table in a shaded Khartoum courtyard in 2186. Outside, the depot keeps working: a League frame, Kafila carriers and the water queue.

UNEL.c: A lunar yard turned relief port after the war. Suited crews pass medical and rebuilding cargo through pressure locks while people inside watch a convoy leave for Earth.

wS5.c: The Great Sand Sea at dusk in 2183. Three sets of supply tracks meet at a wrecked depot among burnt-out hulls, and one Sirocco still works there. The Jinn is nowhere in sight.

fn1.c: An NK-12 stands knee-deep at an Indian field station in monsoon rain. Engineers check the cooling plumbing behind its big radiator grilles and rubber joint boots. Nashik rebuilt that cooling system twice before Moscow agreed it needed rebuilding.

fg3.c: During an evacuation drill outside Tunis, an Elissa kneels behind its rescue shield. Medics load a stretcher into one of the four pods racked behind its hips.

ac26.c: Hawa Abdelrahman's Sirocco faces the Jinn in the Great Sand Sea, the second time they meet. The Jinn stands more than twice its height. This time she lowers her gun.

xb1.c: In a cold Canadian hangar, the Aurora's upper half hangs on crane slings above its legs, two metres short of the waist ring. Calgary built the legs and Montreal the torso. When Canada splits, the halves end up on opposite sides of the line.

yg51.c: Inside a Hospital Safina well behind the North African Front, the old mech bays hold quiet wards. Behind a screen, the graft vats work.

yh51.c: The Hakobune rises on its fans over a storm-damaged Japanese coast. Two Kizunas wait in its open rescue hangar. It carries no weapons.

og_tng.h: Everyone eats at the same table
og_tng.c: The Tangier collective shares one long meal in the shipbreaking yard, mechanics and volunteers together. The half-built Tramuntana stands behind them, its curved hull ribs already part of its body.

xq1.c: The Tramuntana stands guard on a Tangier quay while families board the ferries across the strait.

wO8.h: Survey camp, according to the manifest
wO8.c: Melas Chasma, 2186. A small camp in Ascension's old livery digs a careful trench at the old ████████ site, dwarfed by the canyon wall. On paper it is a survey.

xl1.c: At the south-pole yard, the crews build their own Custodian on a slipway between two half-finished ships from different blocs. Its armour is patched from all of them, every insignia ground off.

o9.c: 2186. Company depot open day: the Concord's pilot pair climb while recruits pass through implant screening. One recruit is quietly led aside.

wW14.c: 2186. At Malapert, Union and British crews join the first keel section of Britain's orbital hull.

o39.c: 2186. The network moves a train of frames on schedule. Beyond its lights, steppe crews watch the crossing.

xk3.c: 2180s. At Nashik, pilots return their augmentation harnesses to the shared rack; the transfer capsule remains unopened.

o46.c: 2186. A Harmattan shelters a water point from the haboob, supplying water and medical care in its lee.

wS14.c: 2177. White-painted donated frames escort food through the Copperbelt as a League checkpoint lets them pass.

wO18.c: 2182. On the drowned Gulf coast, applicants bring the skills and equipment that might sustain a settlement on Mars.

wO22.c: 2186. Judges and river officers hear both banks at one table beside the shrinking Rio Bravo.

wO20.c: In the war. Beneath Strasbourg, the ethics panel keeps reading; one member looks up at the map of Mars.

wO6.c: 2186. Three generations keep the family tender's records, knowledge and continuity contract in the asteroid belt.

xm9.c: 2186. At an oasis, keepers treat the Jinn and patients while distant watchers study the culture vats.

wE15.c: In the war. At Vladivostok, envoys bless the departing pilots and engineers beneath the rescue ark.

wW17.c: In the war. Refugees cross the Arctic sea ice toward the Hearth; the distant sun is only a pale band.

frames.label: Frames
frames.intro: The frame took war back to where it started: humanoid wrestling humanoid in the dust. After the war a few Earth frames are sealed for space and become the space factions' first fleets, and their own makers start by rebuilding those.
turns: There were no mechs yet, only the industries that would build them. Halcyon made jets, Brannock-Hale tanks, Tianlong excavators and Mitsurugi rescue robots, and logging crews walked hydraulic rigs up hillsides. Every frame since has borrowed its parts from one of them.

Brannock-Hale put a construction walker's legs under a tank's armour, and the M4 was slow, loud and very hard to kill. Halcyon, VEK, Boreal and the League's workshops all licensed or rebuilt it, while Tianlong went its own way with the Tieniu. A dozen hand-built Merlins proved a frame could fly.

The blocs stopped borrowing and built for their own wars. The Kestrel cut transformation to two seconds and ran on swap batteries. The Tieshan went the other way: simple, armoured and built in thousands. The Haubert took any role overnight on standard hardpoints. You could tell a bloc by its outline.

These frames answer what Gen 2 taught. The Harrier carries a laser to survive the anti-air rockets, the Bulwark holds the swap points Kestrels depend on, the Mamont opens the gaps, and the Pavise blinds before it shoots. Frames start coming from places nobody planned for: Nashik and, by 2183, the Moon.

Every prototype is built around something the last generation couldn't do: a beam weapon, a reactor, beamed power, a network in place of a pilot, a sworn pair, no legs at all. Most exist in ones and twos, and it isn't yet clear which of them is the future.
The war puts Gen 4's ideas into production: fission in the Burya, capacitors built for Beijing in the Kagerō, and a Kestrel flying on a ration of American parts.
Only a handful of Earth frames are sealed for space, the Teamster, the Pavise, the Tieshan and the Polaris, and every space faction's first fleet is one of them.
Around the Martian crisis, Colony One, the MRD, the Syndicate, Umoja, the Ashva Compact and the Communion build their first frames of their own.
fams: Tanks with legs, built to be fixed with a wrench.
Modular knights, and hand-built frames for aces.
Fast frames from a workers' collective in a squatted hangar, with the drawings free to anyone who asks.
Cold-weather frames from a country that buys from both blocs.
Iron mountains, in their thousands, and lately the network that moves them.
Herder-mechanics' fast frames from the Darkhan rail sheds, joined late by Berlin's splinter.
Heavy, aggressive, and few. Built in Russia, and now in India.
OKB-7's Indian line, learning to build frames for sworn pilots.
Rescuers first, then the world's best actuators.
Three blocs' parts on one frame, until Khartoum starts designing its own.
French and Italian engineering on the Maghreb coast, and the Charter's second design office.
Built on the Moon for a gravity it doesn't have, and given to the UN.
Colony One's workshops in the north of Mars: hammers first, drawings later.
The MRD's design bureau at Vesta, where every frame is a published argument.
The Syndicate's yards at Pallas, building frames to be bought and sold.
Umoja's frames, part built and part grown.
The Ashva Compact's foundry at Europa: Nashik's paired frames and Mitsurugi's hands.
The Communion's engineers, who keep old machines walking in the far dark.
The Constitutionalists' frames: American designs, built under the charter.
Seen, photographed or recovered, and claimed by no maker. Designations are whatever the people who saw them wrote down.
frames.profileH: Who flies what after the war

profile.t: Quiet battery flyers and the Gyrfalcon that flies in vacuum too; turbine heavies from the Steward to the Keystone; Monterrey's Vaquero in the south and Boreal West's Wapiti in the north; Teamster conversions sent to Mars; the Dropguards that take Phobos.

Fuel-cell knights from the Bastide to the Bannerette, Castellani's hand-built aces, Funkenwerk's open-drawing and pack frames, Boreal East in the Arctic, Bastides built in Tunis, and the Pavise conversion it handed to Mars.

Networked companies under one officer, the Iron Ox back at work on aid missions, Khiimori's steppe frames, Mitsurugi building rescue frames and Belt patrol frames for Beijing, converted Tieshans for the houses, and the first fusion frame.
Oath-sworn Volks and Vityaz knights on diesel at home, Nashik's monsoon heavies and sworn pairs, sealed Volks at Venus, and fission Buryas kept off-world.
Desert-turbine frames sold to half of Earth, and the Tunis Works' medic frames for the Charter.
White squads on beamed power, firebreak frames for a healing planet, the space frame everyone copies and its sealed successor, and observers that learned to wear armour.
American Teamster conversions rebuilt in Dustline's sheds, frames of its own from 2312, and frames nobody outside has seen since.
The Charter, plus Halcyon and Brannock-Hale frames built under licence, under a law that won't let any of them fight alone.
The Pavise conversion refitted at Vesta, then its own published designs on Lubov cells, and a fusion testbed.
Converted Tieshans, Riggers that keep the books and the Steppe riders' Saddle-S frames, then silent boarding frames on Arsia lithium.
Salvaged frames with grown muscle, then frames grown from the start.
Ashvin pairs rebuilt at Europa, monster-hunters for the radiation belts, and a fusion frame in trials.
Polaris frames kept walking for a century, frames built to wait, and frames that tend the mirrors.

nodes.t: Halcyon's jet lineage
nodes.x: Halcyon's fighter and ground-attack jets, the company's business before it built a single frame. The wing binders, avionics and flight-control software in every Halcyon frame descend from them.

nodes.t: First variable frame; transformed slowly
nodes.x: The first mech that could fold itself into a flight mode, though not quickly: transformation took eleven seconds, and the tethered LR-1 had to be stowed before it could begin. Only a dozen were built, and that was enough to prove the idea.

nodes.t: Licensed Garrison, lightened for air drops
nodes.x: Halcyon's first mech was a licensed Brannock M4 Garrison with its armour cut back so a tiltrotor could carry it. Brannock-Hale, and the Army officers who had chosen the Garrison, took a long time to forgive Halcyon for improving on it.

nodes.t: America's signature variable frame
nodes.x: The Merlin's flight mode on the Sparrowhawk's ground frame, with the transformation brought down to two seconds. A quick-swap battery spine drives electric ducted fans in the calf nacelles, and it carries an LR-3 in hand. Its forty-minute endurance went on to define US doctrine.

nodes.t: Heavier strike Kestrel with point defence
nodes.x: A bigger Kestrel with QX-3 packs, more wing stores and a PL-2 laser, built to survive the Pact's anti-air rockets and the Sapsans' missiles. It is slightly slower to transform and much harder to shoot down, and after Svalbard it stopped being an option and became the standard.

nodes.t: Swap-pit support frame with battery crane
nodes.x: A non-transforming frame on the Sparrowhawk line, built to run swap pits, with a battery crane on one arm, an MW-3 microwave emitter on the other, and Brannock hybrid power for endurance. When a pit is attacked, and they often are, the crews fight in them.

nodes.t: Harrier with a microwave power receiver
nodes.x: A Harrier fitted with a dorsal rectenna for the SKYLINE beamed-power trials. Two exist, and one of them has flown for six hours without landing.

nodes.t: Armour, fire control, crew survival
nodes.x: Brannock-Hale's tank business supplied the armour layout, fire control and crew-survival thinking for every frame it builds.

nodes.t: Legged demolition and logging rigs
nodes.x: Hydraulic legged rigs for demolition and logging on steep ground. The first machines to walk at this scale.

nodes.t: The first mech in combat service
nodes.x: A construction walker's legs under a tank's armour and fire control: slow, loud and very hard to kill. Almost every army has licensed, copied or rebuilt it at some point.

nodes.t: Heavy frame that holds swap points
nodes.x: Extra armour and a second Hornet pod, built to seize and hold the swap points the Kestrels depend on. The Army describes it, with some pride, as the frame that keeps the Air Force flying.

nodes.t: The US Army's workhorse
nodes.x: The Garrison redesigned for fire teams: hybrid power that lets it go quiet in ambush, standard Hornet mounts, and a stake driver on the left arm. More Teamsters serve than any other US frame.

nodes.t: Testbed for the turbine-capacitor plant
nodes.x: A Teamster rebuilt around a frame-sized HT-20 plant and the AR-40E electrothermal rifle. It was the Army's attempt to match linear-weapon penetration without having to depend on Halcyon for it.

nodes.t: Sensor masts and quiet hulls
nodes.x: European wheeled reconnaissance vehicles, whose sensor masts and quiet running shaped VEK's priorities.

nodes.t: Licensed Garrison with VEK sensors
nodes.x: A licence-built M4 Garrison with a VEK sensor head, and a submarine-derived fuel cell where the turbine used to be. It was quieter than the original and saw rather further, and it was the first frame to carry a mono-eye.

nodes.t: The standard-hardpoint modular frame
nodes.x: VEK's first clean-sheet design, built around the standard hardpoint and BZ-4 stacks, with rounded knightly armour and a mono-eye on a track. The point of it, as far as the Union's planners were concerned, was that one frame could be reconfigured overnight for any role.

nodes.t: Lance knight of the hunter-killer lance
nodes.x: A heavier Haubert built to close and finish, with reinforced arms for the HEAT lance, a large shield, and BZ-6 reformer stacks so that it can refuel from any truck in any of the Union's armies.

nodes.t: EW and coilgun sniper frame
nodes.x: It carries the Spiegel coilgun, the Union's best EW suite and Fenrir missiles. Under Directive 5 it leads the formation; under Directive 8 it is the frame that takes the kill shot.

nodes.t: Hand-built ace frame on Haubert bones
nodes.x: Castellani's take on the Haubert, with lighter armour, Stack-R racing cells and hand-tuned actuators. Each one is built for a single named ace, and each is painted red and gold.

nodes.t: Plasma-blade prototype for the top ace
nodes.x: Built around the Lama Ardente plasma blade, with Destrier-style arm bracing and a licensed capacitor core in the chest. It fights at full power for about forty seconds.

nodes.t: The Blitz's heir, built in a squatted hangar
nodes.x: Funkenwerk's first frame, from people who thought the Haubert's knight armour was a costume. It is a light runner on a modular cell stack, lighter than an Écuyer and faster than anything else the Union fields on the ground, assembled in open bays at Tempelhof where anyone can walk in and watch. Crews paint their own frames, so no two match. The drawings are public, so a field workshop can fix one with whatever fits. The German and Dutch contingents bought it to screen their columns. Union staff officers called it unprofessional, and Funkenwerk printed that on its posters.

nodes.t: Open-drawing raider that hunts jammers
nodes.x: German for a ricochet, and for someone who won't fall in line. After Svalbard, six collectives in Berlin, Leipzig, Rotterdam, Gdańsk, Lisbon and Marseille built it from one set of public drawings. It runs on a reformer stack that makes its own hydrogen from diesel, so it never waits on a depot the way the Blitz did. Its Fenrir missiles home on jammers, and a pirate-radio rig in the back drowns out everyone else's signals. The Union has never placed an order for one, though between them its national contingents have bought more than a hundred.

nodes.t: The punks grown up: black, sealed and fast
nodes.x: Funkenwerk's first frame built to a state contract, and the one that split the cooperative. When the Union procurement office stalled for a third year, Berlin offered to pay directly, and the members voted 61 to 39 to take the money. The ones who left kept the Querschläger drawings. The ones who stayed built this: the Querschläger grown up, with a sealed, faceted hull, a reformer stack buffered by a licensed capacitor core, and a Spiegel coilgun it can fire on the run. Before it, no two Funkenwerk frames had ever matched, and every Aufbruch is black. Berliners take that as a promise that Germany will stop waiting for the rest of the Union, and Paris takes it the same way, though as a warning. Two are flying.

nodes.t: Rail sheds, rally trucks and herders' motorcycles
nodes.x: Darkhan's railway sheds, the Gobi's rally-truck garages and every herder who keeps a forty-year-old motorcycle running. Khiimori's frames come out of their habits: weld what you have, carry your own spares, and never trust a depot to be there.

nodes.t: Wild horse: a welded-tube runner from the Darkhan sheds
nodes.x: Named for the takhi, the wild horse of the steppe. Darkhan's rail workshops built it for outriders who were wearing out stripped Tieniu on the frame-train routes. It is a welded tube frame like a rally truck's, on long legs from a tracklayer's suspension, with a tractor's multi-fuel diesel and a felt-lined cab big enough to sleep in. The welds are ugly and it rattles at speed, but it is faster than anything else the Pact owns, and any herder's mechanic can fix it. Beijing never placed an order; the outriders bought them straight from the shed.

nodes.t: Eagle: the Takhi grown into a raider
nodes.x: Named for the golden eagles the steppe's hunters fly from the saddle. The Bürged is a Takhi grown into a raider: longer legs, a rocket rack on the back, a carbon blade, and a stooping charge the crews learned from watching the eagles. Its engineering is still Darkhan's, with hand-bent tube, salvaged Tieshan actuators and a diesel tuned past what the manual allows. Outriders ride it a hundred kilometres between depots and fight with whatever they carry, and more than once Moscow's planners have underestimated how far that is.

nodes.t: “White Wind”: the splinter's answer to the Aufbruch
nodes.x: In 2185 the thirty-nine percent who walked out of Funkenwerk over the Berlin contract arrived at Khiimori's sheds with the Querschläger drawings and nowhere else to go. They had sworn never to paint a frame black. The Tsagaan Salkhi is what the two shops built that winter, its sealed armour painted matt white over dark joints, with blue khadag scarves at the shoulders: as unlike the Aufbruch as the splinter could make it. The outriders named it for the tsagaan zud, the white winter that kills a herd in a night. Berlin's sealed panels and reformer stack sit on Darkhan's long legs and stooping charge, and for the first time the welds are clean. The money did not come from a vote. Beijing pays for the machined parts and the shed time, and some of the thirty-nine percent bristle at having walked out on one state's contract only to take another's. It is the fastest frame anyone has built, low and swept back, and it looks like it wants to hurt you. Beijing asked for the drawings, and the collective published them the same week in Mongolian, Mandarin and German. Three are flying.

nodes.t: Arctic mining logistics
nodes.x: Tracked haulers and snow tractors that kept northern mines supplied across winter ice roads. Boreal's heated drivetrains, and its habit of wasting no heat at all, start here.

nodes.t: Licensed Garrison, winterised
nodes.x: Canada's first frames were Brannock M4 Garrisons built under licence in Calgary, and almost every change made to them was about the cold: heated actuators, wide snowshoe feet, and a turbine that would start at forty below. The licence terms were set in Washington, and they were not generous.

nodes.t: Arctic frame on US bones with a Union sensor head
nodes.x: Boreal's first design of its own: a Teamster-pattern chassis on snowshoe feet, a hybrid plant that can idle for a week on one tank of diesel, and a VEK sensor head, bought because Washington wouldn't export its newest one. US officers tend to describe it as a Teamster for people who don't trust the US Army, and Norway was among the buyers, with an order for forty.

nodes.t: Runs as cold as the ice it hides in
nodes.x: Built after Svalbard, where the Union showed that whoever is seen first loses. The Wolverine can lie in the snow for days on a reformer-stack trickle, with an insulated hull and passive sensors, and its thermal signature is close to the ice around it. The fuel cells are Union-pattern, and over the years more and more of its buyers have been Union armies as well.

nodes.t: Sealed long-endurance frame for the high Arctic
nodes.x: Officially it is a search-and-rescue frame, with a sealed cab two people can live in for a month, a heat-recovery loop that wastes almost nothing, and a power budget counted in watts rather than kilowatts. Boreal builds it in both Calgary and Montreal. The Halifax Motion passed the week it was unveiled, and Ottawa and Washington have argued about who owns it ever since; after the partition both plants go on building it, each for its own side.

nodes.t: Diesel construction machinery
nodes.x: Tianlong's civilian excavators and tractors supplied the diesel-electric drive, the hydraulics and the factories.

nodes.t: “Iron Ox”: excavator drive, shoulder cannon
nodes.x: An excavator drive train in an egg-shaped armoured torso, with a tank gun on the shoulder that could only be fired from a kneel. Thousands were built, and many are still in service with the League.

nodes.t: “Iron Mountain”: the most-built mech in the world
nodes.x: Adopted in the same year as the Type-09 cannon it was built to carry. It has thick armour, few moving parts, a cockpit buried deep in the torso and a multi-fuel diesel, and a pilot can be trained for it in about six weeks.

nodes.t: Depot upgrade: radios, optics, drum rifle
nodes.x: Tieshans upgraded at depot level with better radios, optics and Type-07 drum rifles, so older frames can be brought up to standard without new production lines. The new radios also carry Tianshu's data link, which matters more to Beijing's planners than the optics do.

nodes.t: “Light Mountain”: slab armour, long legs, drum rifle
nodes.x: A Tieshan built to keep up with the mountain regiments instead of kneeling for them. A second Tianlong line swapped the cast hull for flat welded slab armour, lengthened the legs and traded the long cannon for a Type-07 drum rifle, with a single rocket tube on the shoulder. It was taller and faster than the Tieshan, and it died faster too: slab plates split where the cast hull would have shrugged off the hit. The line closed after a few thousand were built, but the drum rifle it proved went into every Tieshan-Kai refit.

nodes.t: “Iron Wall”: fortress-belt and anti-air frame
nodes.x: A squat, heavily armoured Tieshan derivative built to be dug in, with a Type-09 cannon and anti-air rocket racks for the Air Umbrella. It walks only as far as its position and is not expected to leave it. Behind the belt, a salt reactor train feeds it by cable while its diesel idles.

nodes.t: “Sky Eye”: one pilot, a Tianshu node, six uncrewed frames
nodes.x: Beijing's answer to augmented pilots was to change the network, not the pilot. A Tieshan-Kai chassis carries a Tianshu node in the torso and an unaugmented pilot, who commands six uncrewed Tieshan conversions that walk wherever Tianshu sends them. The network proposes and the pilot approves. The same node runs the trial frame's Salt Core, so the pilot commands six frames and never touches the power. In trials the uncrewed frames hold a kneeling line better than conscripts do. What happens when the link is jammed has not, so far, been part of the trials.

nodes.t: OKB-7's jet lineage
nodes.x: OKB-7's interceptors and long-range bombers. Its first frame took their landing gear, their twin cannon and their control laws, and it dropped from their bomb bays.

nodes.t: Airborne raider on interceptor landing gear
nodes.x: OKB-7's first frame, built for the Pact's airborne divisions and dropped by parachute platform from converted bombers. Its legs are interceptor landing-gear forgings: long oleo struts that soak up a hard landing and give it a loping run no Tieniu could match. Its control laws came straight from the Strizh with the limits left off - fine for a fighter pilot in a g-suit, less so for a Korsak pilot, who doesn't have one. At Talysh the drop scattered across the passes, and several frames were recovered with their pilots unconscious in the seat. Fewer than ninety were built before the airborne divisions went back to light tanks. OKB-7 kept the control laws on file. The Rys flew them again, and the Volk is what they became once Department Zero had pilots who could take them.

nodes.t: Enlarged Tieshan chassis, built-in guns
nodes.x: OKB-7 enlarged the Tieshan chassis, fitted twin diesels, built a rotary cannon into each forearm and added a Grad-M battery. It was the Pact's first frame built for quality rather than numbers, and since the Delhi Accession a second OKB-7 line at Nashik has built them too.

nodes.t: Breakthrough heavy with integral maul arm
nodes.x: The breakthrough frame, with an enormous articulated steel maul for a right arm, a rotary in the left forearm, a Grad-M battery and armour that rifle fire does very little to. Its job is to break the barriers so that the waves behind it can pour through.

nodes.t: Elite rail frame for augmented pilots
nodes.x: A lighter, faster Medved derivative with a Type-12 rail rifle and a KN-1 capacitor. Its control system assumes an augmented pilot, and ordinary pilots black out in it. Beijing will not rewrite its pilots, and so has never fielded one.

nodes.t: Siege frame: Kalibr-305 or Iskra
nodes.x: The heaviest conventional frame ever built. It anchors itself with spades and fires the Kalibr-305, or carries the Iskra particle cannon fed by cable from an MTU-7 truck.

nodes.t: Fission-powered test frame
nodes.x: A Mamont chassis carrying the Pamir micro-reactor. It can run for weeks. Its pilots' radiation exposure is a state secret: ███ mSv per sortie. Test pilots assigned: ██. Still flying: █.

nodes.t: India's licence-production tradition
nodes.x: Decades of Indian factories building foreign fighters and tanks under licence, and learning more from each contract than the licensor meant to teach.

nodes.t: OKB-7's heavy frame, rebuilt for heat and monsoon
nodes.x: The price of the Delhi Accession: Medveds built at Nashik under OKB-7 supervision, with sealed joints for the monsoon, larger radiators for the plains, and Indian crews for the breakthrough groups. Nashik's engineers rebuilt the cooling system twice before Moscow agreed it needed rebuilding.

nodes.t: Paired frames for oath-sworn pilots
nodes.x: Nashik's first clean-sheet design, built around the Nashik Oath rather than Department Zero: two lighter, Volk-derived frames that fight as a sworn pair, linked so that each pilot sees what the other sees. The augmentation is worn rather than implanted, a pilot rig that comes off after the ride and goes back to the unit store. The frames take their name from the Ashvins, the twin divine horsemen of the old stories. Moscow wants the pair for the breakthrough groups; their pilots want them for the line.

nodes.t: Bought from the rival, maintained on its schedule
nodes.x: In 2173, after a decade of raids it couldn't answer and a ridge it had to give up, Delhi bought the only frames anyone would sell it quickly: export Tieshans from Tianlong, the same model that had knelt above the Ladakh pass. Indian depots added bigger radiators and a second radio. Everything else came from China, and spares came only through Tianlong's export depots, released when Tianshu scheduled them. Indian crews learned more from the Tieshan than Tianlong meant to teach. They also learned what it is to wait for a Chinese network to decide when your frame can walk. In 2186, a week after the Sealed Session, the schedule stopped.

nodes.t: Japanese disaster robotics
nodes.x: Decades of Japanese work on rescue robots and powered exoskeletons, the origin of Mitsurugi's lead in actuators and balance control.

nodes.t: Unarmed disaster-response frame
nodes.x: An unarmed rescue frame for earthquakes and tsunamis, with the best balance control and hands in the world. The Japanese public met mechs as rescuers first, and for a good many people in Japan that first impression has stayed.

nodes.t: JSDF coastal-defence frame
nodes.x: A clean humanoid frame for coast and island defence, with hybrid cells, a Type-L coil carbine and an HF-1 sonic blade. It is understated on the outside, and the actuators inside are superb.

nodes.t: Upgraded Hayate for live test units
nodes.x: A Hayate with spare power and enough mounts for whatever prototype the lab sends next, flown by the live test units.

nodes.t: First frame built around a beam weapon
nodes.x: A Shiden rebuilt around one weapon, and lopsided because of it: a braced right shoulder and forearm cradle for the BX-0 emitter, and a cooling module on the left of the back with thermal cartridges the ground crew swap between test strings. It's the first frame designed around an energy weapon rather than adapted to carry one, with a Mk.III core behind the right chest. Clean white with blue and red accents, and no crest. One exists, and every bloc's intelligence service knows where it is kept.

nodes.t: Rebuilt Garrisons and Tieniu
nodes.x: Surplus M4 Garrisons and Type-01 Tieniu, rebuilt in League workshops with sand filters and whatever parts could be found. Everything the company built later started on those benches.

nodes.t: Tieniu torso on Garrison legs
nodes.x: Qadira's first production frame: a licensed Tieniu torso on Garrison-pattern legs with wide desert feet. It was ugly and reliable, and the League has stuck with that way of doing things ever since, as its crews are happy to tell you.

nodes.t: Q-Mix turbine, VEK-pattern sensors
nodes.x: The current League frame: a Q-Mix turbine, second-hand VEK sensor heads, and mounts that take US or Eurasian pods. Every part is sourced from at least two blocs, so no single embargo can ground it.

nodes.t: Kestrel airframe, VEK sensors, MHI blade
nodes.x: Grey Lantern builds from bought and stolen parts: a Kestrel airframe with the transformation removed, a VEK sensor head, an MHI sonic blade. No two are alike, and none are legal.

nodes.t: Built in Khartoum to hold ground and shelter people
nodes.x: The first Qadira frame designed in Khartoum instead of assembled from three blocs' parts: a Sirocco chassis with a sealed cab, a dozer-blade shield wide enough to cover a family, water panniers and ground-level first-aid support, and a Q-Mix turbine re-tuned for local fuels. Its designers spent a month in the Great Sand Sea watching how the Jinn moves among people. In Khartoum they say it is the line the League will keep building after it stops being a league.

nodes.t: Building to European licence
nodes.x: Shipyards in Tunis and Bizerte, and rail works in Algiers, that built ferries, rolling stock and tractors under French and Italian licence for most of a century. Their engineers learned the European way of doing things, licences and inspections included, while keeping the old Carthaginian habit of trading with everyone.

nodes.t: Haubert built in Tunis for the Union's partners
nodes.x: After the Maghreb Depot Strikes, Strasbourg promised its North African partners they would never again be left blind or stranded, and opened a Haubert line in Tunis to prove it: sealed joints, sand filters, a dust-shielded mono-eye track and a finish of sand and slate. French engineers ran the plant. Tunisian and Algerian crews built and flew the frames, and named them after the wind from the north.

nodes.t: Castellani's craft for desert lances
nodes.x: Castellani opened a workshop beside the Tunis line to build Falcos for the partner states' aces, then a cheaper frame for the rest of their lances: Falco-pattern actuators, BZ-6 stacks that refuel from any truck, and a tall sensor mast for the open desert. Its Tunisian pilots gave it the Italian name for the hot wind off the Sahara, and the Italian engineers who came out for three years have, for the most part, now been there for ten.

nodes.t: The Charter's first frame from Tunis
nodes.x: When the Maghreb signed the Khartoum Charter, the Tunis works went with it, and so did most of the French and Italian engineers who ran them. Under Qadira they are building a frame that keeps the Union's standard hardpoints and Castellani's hand-tuned joints on a chassis built for Protect First: a shield arm, an evacuation cradle on the back, and room in the cab for a medic. It is named after Carthage's founding queen. Strasbourg wants its licences back, and has said so in writing.

nodes.t: Crewed orbital work pods
nodes.x: One-person pods with manipulator arms that built the first stations.

nodes.t: Four-armed worker frame
nodes.x: Four arms, vestigial legs used as anchors, and a big thruster pack. The standard station worker frame, and the one the workers armed in the labour dispute.

nodes.t: Long-duration salvage frame
nodes.x: A bigger worker frame with solar-fuel power for multi-day shifts and a tether harpoon for salvage. Safety yellow with hazard stripes.

nodes.t: Militarised Rigger with spike driver
nodes.x: Sold as a station-security variant. In practice it is a Rigger with armour plates, an RD-12 spike driver and a boarding harpoon, and every bloc has bought some, which has done the seller's books no harm at all.

nodes.t: First purpose-built space combat frame
nodes.x: Built for the catapults of the first warships, with no legs, and with a Halcyon linear rifle where the construction tools would be. No one yet knows quite how it should fight, and its first instructor is writing the manual as he goes, logging each change.

nodes.t: Luna's first frame built for Earth
nodes.x: The first frame the lunar foundries built for a gravity they don't have: vacuum-cast titanium-foam armour, Rigger joints rebuilt for six times the load, an ice-water fuel cell, and a sealed cockpit with its own air for smoke, gas and fallout. A rescue cradle folds out of the chest. Luna couldn't test it, so it was tested in the Atacama. The Republic gave the first twelve to the UN in 2183 as a gift, white from the foundry and armed with whatever Geneva chose to fit, and they went to the white squads' best crews. For the Republic it was a way of making its case to the UN in hardware rather than speeches.

nodes.t: A firebreak frame for a burning planet
nodes.x: A Tellus rebuilt for the fires that come every summer now: mirror-finished heat shields that throw back radiant heat, a dozer blade and trenching cutters for cutting firebreaks, and water bladders on the back that it fills from any river. From Shackleton the fire seasons show up on the Earth's face as brown smudges, and the Republic built the Albedo for them. The white squads first took it to the fire lines in Provence and Liguria in 2184, and the Union's own fire services asked to borrow two.

nodes.t: Ring power for the white squads' best
nodes.x: The Republic's prototype for the best pilots in the white squads: a Tellus rebuilt around a rectenna that draws beamed power from the Republic's own relay satellites, which it has offered to park over any UN operation. Under the relay it never runs dry; away from one it falls back on the Tellus's ice-water cell. It carries a lunar-built coil carbine, a tether harpoon and a sealed rescue capsule for four in the chest. Two have been built, and after Mong Hsat one was refitted as the Defender: heavier plate, a tall shelter shield and a heavy coil rifle, built to stand between incoming fire and an evacuation. Stencilled inside the cockpit hatch, in the Republic's own lettering: space is dark and cold without it.

nodes.t: Seen once, behind the Pact line at Talysh
nodes.x: Photographed in 2169 behind the Pact line at the Battle of the Talysh Mountains, recovering wrecked Tieniu cores rather than fighting. US photo interpreters noted a cockpit with no canopy and no hatch, cooling lines running into the seat, and Cyrillic stencils ground off and painted over. Its leg forgings match OKB-7's interceptor landing gear. File status: ██████████ ██ ████████.

nodes.t: The two frames left in the surf at Yonaguni
nodes.x: Two of the frames from the Yaeyama Incidents were left behind in the surf. Their cast hull armour has weld seams like Tianlong's, but the welds are robot-laid, which Tianlong's plants weren't supposed to manage until 2179. They carried drum-fed rifles with Type-07 rifling, and radios with no maker's marks on a frequency plan that no one in the Pact admits to. Japan kept both hulls, published nothing and, as far as anyone can tell, asked no one about them. Present location of hulls: ██████ ███████ ███████.

nodes.t: The frame that carried the Raijin break-in team
nodes.x: Found abandoned in a drainage culvert two kilometres from the Tsukuyomi Lab perimeter. It had Halcyon-pattern wing-binder hinges with the part numbers drilled out, a Vauclair-Ehrlich sensor head, and radar-absorbent panelling that isn't in Grey Lantern's catalogue. The captured contractor said it arrived by container and he never saw who loaded it. Halcyon's reply to Japan's inquiry was ███ █████ ███ ██████.

nodes.t: Four arms, a core drill, and nobody's survey
nodes.x: A Colony One survey drone photographed it at the bottom of Melas Chasma: a four-armed frame with Rigger shoulders, a core drill where a manipulator should be, and a sealed cargo pod with refrigeration fins on its back. Ascension's last inventory lists no frame of that description. The drone's next three passes were jammed. Contents of cargo pod: ████████.

nodes.t: A restraint frame with nothing in it
nodes.x: Swiss customs photographs of a crate bound for Marseille: a load-bearing exoframe with joint brakes and an armoured cab in the chest, the same pattern as the Field Cohort's, but built for something much larger, and empty. The consignee was a shipping agent in ████████. Halden told the ethics panel the frame was surplus. It did not say surplus to what.

nodes.t: Raid frames that move like something alive
nodes.x: Indian Army designation for the frames that came ashore at Ratnagiri in 2180 and burned the fuel depot in forty minutes. Garrison hips and a Tieniu torso welded together the way the desert workshops build Haboobs, but the limbs are sheathed in bundles of grey-red fibre that tighten and relax like muscle. Engineers who recovered a severed forearm found polymer strands soaked in a nutrient gel, and logged that it was still warm two days later. The pilots keep fighting after wounds that should stop them. The soldiers called them rakshasa, demons, and the name stuck in the files. The crews are the monsoon bands. Origin of fibre: ███████ ███████ ██ ███ ████.

nodes.t: Its wounds closed between photographs
nodes.x: Photographed twice by a League coastal patrol at Ras Hafun, a week apart, months after the Kafila ambush, beside a dhow-ferry loading for the crossing to India. In the first photograph its left thigh is torn open to the frame. In the second the wound has closed under a ridged, pinkish sheath. The muscle bundles are the Rakshasa's pattern, but these carry no gel lines. Khartoum's medical council asked to see the photographs, then asked who else had seen them. The keepers recognised the crew. Present location: ████████.

nodes.t: One frame, one voice, and no heat in the cab
nodes.x: Seen once, in 2186, after a landslide buried a hill village above Makassar. Before the provincial rescue teams arrived, a grey frame of ordinary size had dug out thirty-six people and laid them in a row along the road, then walked into the forest. Its parts came from three blocs. Survivors said it paused before every choice, briefly, the way one person thinks rather than the way a crew confers. A rescue drone's thermal camera found no heat in the cab. The designation is the one stencilled on a crate at the Makassar pump works the following week. Occupant: ███████.

nodes.t: The Kestrel on a ration
nodes.x: The war's Kestrel, a Harrier airframe flying on the QX-5 pack and a Liberty Core once the Mitsurugi parts stopped coming. It manages thirty-one minutes in the air and carries a linear rifle that fails in desert heat. American pilots fly it anyway, since there is nothing else to fly.

nodes.t: The Teamster rebuilt for a long war
nodes.x: Brannock-Hale's war frame: a Teamster with the Pathfinder's turbine-capacitor plant, a Liberty Core, and armour for a war that no one had expected to last. It is slow and loud, the Monterrey plant builds it by the tens of thousands, and it holds both the Central American and Canadian fronts.

nodes.t: The Union's last frame of the war
nodes.x: VEK's wartime knight, built for the European Front on the BZ-8 field reformer, which runs on whatever fuel is left. It combines the Destrier's lance role with the Pavise's jammers, a compromise reached because by the second year the Union can no longer afford two frames.

nodes.t: Canadians on both sides of the Winter War
nodes.x: Boreal's last design before the partition splits the company, a bog-footed cold-weather frame that both halves go on building, one to Washington's specification and the other to Strasbourg's. When the Winter War comes, it is fought in Muskegs on both sides of the line, and by Canadians on both sides too.

nodes.t: “War Mountain”: built faster than it could be painted
nodes.x: The Tieshan simplified again for the Pact Civil War, built in bare metal on siege diesels and sent to the front by rail in the thousands. Both halves of the Pact field it, and both paint their own stars on it at the depot.

nodes.t: The Pamir in production, for the siege trains
nodes.x: OKB-7 puts the Pamir's fission core into a production heavy frame and sends it north with the siege trains. It never needs refuelling, and its pilots are rotated out when they reach their radiation dose rather than when the fighting stops. The Mandate's ban on battlefield reactors is written with the Burya in mind.

nodes.t: Built in Osaka, for Beijing
nodes.x: Mitsurugi's war frame, and the first it builds to Tianlong's schedule under Beijing's protection. It carries the Mk.IV capacitor the West can no longer buy, and it is flown for China by Japanese crews who signed up to defend Japan.

nodes.t: The North African Front's frame
nodes.x: Khartoum's war frame, a Harmattan heavied up for the North African Front. It shelters refugees from the Southern Crossing as readily as it fights, and when the African Commonwealth's founders talk about the war, it is the frame they tend to remember.

nodes.t: A frame for the open cities
nodes.x: Shackleton Works' war frame for the white squads, built to stand at the edge of an open city and be seen there. It is white, lit and lightly armed, and the squads' logs record that for the most part the fronts go round it.

nodes.t: The first space combat frame built in numbers
nodes.x: The Marlinspike in production at the lunar yard, sold to every bloc for the Orbital Front, which was good business whichever side was winning. Its boarding spike and reaction thrusters set the pattern for every frame that has fought in vacuum since.

nodes.t: Quiet again, on two hours of lithium
nodes.x: With lithium shipped down from space and capacitors from the lunar yards, Halcyon builds the frame it always wanted: a quiet battery flyer with two hours in the air. It is America's frame for the peace, and the Kestrel line's last on Earth.

nodes.t: The reconstruction's heavy hand
nodes.x: The Ironside's peacetime heir, built for garrisons and reconstruction on cheap fuel shipped down from the Belt. It holds the Andean border through the Federation's collapse and the Bolivian annexation.

nodes.t: The Teamster sealed for Mars, and Colony One's first frame
nodes.x: One of the few Earth frames given a space conversion: a Teamster with a sealed cab, cold-rated actuators and a Martian cold cell. Washington sends them to Colony One by the hundred, and for a century most of Colony One's frames start life as one.

nodes.t: The Union's peace frame, on Quebec hydrogen
nodes.x: The refounded Union's standard frame. It is modular like the Haubert, fuelled from the Quebec fields, and built to be exactly the same frame whether it comes off the line in Lisbon, Warsaw or Montreal.

nodes.t: The Pavise sealed for Mars, and the MRD's first frame
nodes.x: The Union's other space conversion: the Pavise jammer frame sealed for Mars and handed to the station that became the MRD. The MRD keeps it for a century and argues with Strasbourg about every refit.

nodes.t: One officer, a Tianshu node and a company of frames
nodes.x: The Tianyan grown up: one officer in a command frame, a Tianshu node in its chest and twelve uncrewed Tieshans around it. It is how China garrisons its sphere after the war, and the Córdoba protests are about it.

nodes.t: The Iron Mountain in vacuum, and the houses' first frame
nodes.x: Tianlong's space conversion of the Tieshan, built for its Belt stations and sold or leased to the Syndicate's houses. Most house frames for a century are Tieshan-S hulls under house paint.

nodes.t: For oath-sworn pilots, on diesel
nodes.x: The Ascendancy's Earth frame after the Mandate: a Volk built for pilots sworn to the Nashik Oath, running on twin diesels now that reactors are banned from Earth's battlefields. The fission frames have not gone anywhere; the Ascendancy simply keeps them off-world.

nodes.t: Sealed for the cloud stations at Venus
nodes.x: The Volk sealed against acid and pressure for the Ascendancy's Venus stations, charged from their solar banks. The UNEL has only ever seen them in long-range imagery.

nodes.t: Sold to half of Earth
nodes.x: The Commonwealth's export frame, built around the desert turbine and sold to every government and warlord rebuilding after the war. In South America, both sides of most borders fly it.

nodes.t: The white squads on the UNEL's relay
nodes.x: The white squads' frame for the reconstruction. It is charged by the UNEL's beamed-power relays wherever it goes, and it can be switched off from Luna if it goes somewhere it should not.

nodes.t: The space frame everyone copies
nodes.x: The UNEL's standard space frame, built in the lunar yards and licensed to every navy. Most space frames of the next century are Grapnels or copies of one.

nodes.t: The high-Arctic frame that went further
nodes.x: The Polaris was built for the high Arctic, and the Polar Exodus carried it into space. Sealed, slow and made to idle for weeks at a time, it is the frame in which the Communion walked out into the far dark, and in which it walks there still.

nodes.t: Colony One's Teamster-S, rebuilt with a hammer
nodes.x: Dustline Works starts as Colony One's repair sheds. Washington's Teamster-S frames have to be kept running long after Washington stops sending spares, so the sheds make their own. By the 2250s a Dust Teamster has almost nothing American left in it.

nodes.t: Vesta's refit of the Pavise-S
nodes.x: The MRD's first design office, at its Vesta station, starts by refitting the Union's Pavise-S and publishing every change for the panels to review. The Proof is the result: in hardware terms much the same frame, but with every decision written down and open to challenge.

nodes.t: A Rigger that keeps the books
nodes.x: Skycut Foundry, at Pallas, builds its first frames on Ascension's old Rigger: worker frames for the houses, each with a counting rig in the cab, because a house frame records every tonne it moves and the house likes to know what it is owed.

nodes.t: Grown muscle on a salvaged frame
nodes.x: Umoja's first frames are salvaged hulls, their actuators replaced by the keepers with grown muscle and vat electrocyte cells. A Kinsman heals small damage on its own, and like anything grown it has to be fed and cared for.

nodes.t: The paired frames, rebuilt at Europa
nodes.x: Garuda Works begins by rebuilding the Nashik pilots' paired frames at Europa, with actuators from the Mitsurugi exiles and ice-water fuel cells. The pairs who ride them are sworn to the Oath, just as the first Ashvins were.

nodes.t: Polaris-S hulls kept walking for a century
nodes.x: The Hearthwrights rebuild the same Polaris-S frames again and again, generation after generation, and no hull is ever quite let go. An Ember is a Polaris-S with a century of repairs in it, and a name painted on it by every pilot who has flown it.

nodes.t: Hot-dropped from Phobos
nodes.x: The US Rapid Defence Force's frame on Phobos: a Teamster-S successor built to drop from orbit onto Mars at a few hours' notice. In July 2312 they take Phobos with almost no fighting.

nodes.t: The Union's Tier One frame for boarding stations
nodes.x: Built for the Union's Tier One units: a compact Bastide for corridors, docking spines and station control rooms, places the Haubert's knightly bulk was never meant to fit. In 2312 it goes to Cyprus and to Deimos.

nodes.t: The networked company in vacuum
nodes.x: The Tianyan-Hou sealed for space, with a Tianshu node running a company of uncrewed Tieshan-S. China's Belt patrols fly them, and its marines board pirate ships behind them.

nodes.t: Unarmed, very visible, sent where the UNEL wants witnesses
nodes.x: The UNEL's answer to the Martian civil war: a frame with no weapons, white paint and every camera it can carry, crewed by volunteers who will fly it into a no-fly zone to see who fires.

nodes.t: Colony One's first frame of its own
nodes.x: Dustline's first original design. Built for the war Colony One had been planning against the MRD: armoured, cold-rated and repairable in a tunnel. When the fleet falls, it goes into the partisan war.

nodes.t: The MRD's first original design
nodes.x: Vesta Works' first frame of its own, built on Ana Lubov's metallic-hydrogen cell, with every drawing published for the panels. It fights the Martian civil war at range, which is how the MRD generally prefers to fight when it has the choice.

nodes.t: A boarding frame that runs silent on Arsia lithium
nodes.x: Skycut's first combat design: a small, silent boarding frame for the houses' stop-and-search campaign against American shipping, running on cheap Arsia packs.

nodes.t: The first frame Umoja grew from the start
nodes.x: There is no salvaged hull in a Kith. Its frame is printed and its muscle grown alongside it, so that the frame and its power were never separate things, and the keepers tend it as one body.

nodes.t: A monster-hunter's frame for the radiation belts
nodes.x: Garuda Works' first original design, built for the Compact's hunters in Jupiter's radiation belts. It is heavily shielded, paired like the Ashvins, and armed for things a good deal bigger than frames.

nodes.t: Built to wait a decade between fights
nodes.x: The Hearthwrights' first new frame in a century, made to sleep for years on a trickle of power through the long cold and to wake ready when it is called. The Communion's frames rarely fight, and they are not built to hurry.

nodes.t: It can't deploy without Washington's code
nodes.x: New Philadelphia Arsenal's first frame: American design, built under the charter, with a deployment lock that only Washington can release. For the Constitutionalists the lock is the point - a promise to Washington that no Martian war will start without it.

nodes.t: Built in the hidden docks, never shown
nodes.x: Dustline's designers go with the remnant to its hidden docks and build frames there that no one outside has photographed. The crews train in the dark. Washington takes the rumour seriously.

nodes.t: The MRD's standard frame after the war
nodes.x: The Theorem made reliable, with Lubov's cell tamed by another team, as tends to happen with her work, and every frame in the MRD's two thirds of Mars built to it.

nodes.t: Guard frames for the Great Exchange
nodes.x: Skycut's frame for guarding the Syndicate's exchanges at Pallas, Juno and Ceres. It is well armed, very visible, and paid for out of the trades it protects.

nodes.t: Lined with mats that eat Jupiter's radiation
nodes.x: Umoja's frame for Ganymede's surface, lined with radiotroph mats that feed on the same radiation that would cripple any other faction's frame. What is grown is cared for, and the mats are tended like the rest of it.

nodes.t: The frame that tends the Long Mirrors
nodes.x: A light, long-armed frame for tending the kilometre mirrors at Uranus. The Communion's pilots treat the work as devotion, and keep the mirrors as others keep a watch, through the cold and the long dark.

nodes.t: The first frame on a fusion core
nodes.x: Tianlong's first frame built around the Type-50 fusion core, in trials in 2327. It needs no fuel, no battery and no relay. If the trials go well, a frame's power plant will no longer decide how it has to fight, which has been true of every frame since the Garrison.

nodes.t: The Compact's fusion frame
nodes.x: Garuda Works' answer to the Zhulong, built around a frame fusion core of the Compact's own, and the riders who test it are confident they will have it flying first.

nodes.t: A frame for a fusion cell that works for minutes
nodes.x: Vesta Works' testbed for the MRD's catalysed fusion cell. It walks for minutes at a time, and every minute is published.

nodes.t: Civil rescue frame on the Osprey's bones
nodes.x: Halcyon's offshoot for the reconstruction: the Osprey's swap-pit crane frame rebuilt as an unarmed rescue and logistics frame, sold to aid agencies, the UNEL and anyone rebuilding a city. More Osprey-Cs are flying in 2312 than Peregrines.

nodes.t: Halcyon's first frame for vacuum and air alike
nodes.x: Halcyon's answer to the Martian crisis: a variable frame that transforms for flight in the air of Earth and Mars and flies on thrusters in vacuum, on orbital lithium and lunar capacitors. It is the first Halcyon frame built under licence by the Constitutionalists as well as at home, and for New Philadelphia that licence matters as much as the frame.

nodes.t: Brannock-Hale Monterrey's light frame for the south
nodes.x: Brannock-Hale's Monterrey plant designs its own light frame for Mexico and Central America: fast, cheap and built to be fixed on a ranch. The Bolivian annexation rolls in on Vaqueros, and they turn up on every side of every border south of the Rio Bravo, not always through the front door.

nodes.t: The heavy frame of 2327
nodes.x: Brannock-Hale's heavy for the Greater Solar Crisis: built for vacuum, Mars and Earth alike, with the Dropguard's drop gear and the Steward's armour. It is the first Brannock-Hale frame designed with New Philadelphia's arsenal as a licensed second source.

nodes.t: Castellani's hand-built frame for the Union's aces
nodes.x: Castellani never stopped building one frame at a time. The Aquila is its post-war ace frame, hand-built on Bastide bones for the handful of Union pilots famous enough to get one, and the first Castellani rated for vacuum.

nodes.t: The Union's frame for 2327
nodes.x: VEK's frame for the Greater Solar Crisis, built as much for station corridors and Martian dust as for Europe: the Rondache's boarding kit on the Bastide's modular frame. The Union means to hold its anchorages at Deimos and the Trojans with it.

nodes.t: An open-drawing frame for rebuilding
nodes.x: After the war the cooperative goes back to its roots: the Querschläger's open drawings, simplified into a frame any workshop can build from scrap for clearing rubble and rebuilding cities. Copies are built from Lisbon to Lagos, and Funkenwerk asks only that the drawings stay free.

nodes.t: Small frames that fight in packs
nodes.x: The Aufbruch line's heir, from the state-contract half of the cooperative: a dozen small frames run as one pack, built for the boarding actions and station fights the Union now has to plan for. The open-drawing half calls it a betrayal, though the two halves still sit and vote together at the cooperative's general meetings.

nodes.t: Boreal West, building for Washington
nodes.x: When Boreal splits into Boreal West and Boreal East, Calgary keeps the Muskeg's drawings and builds this: a cold-weather frame on American batteries for Western Canada and Alaska, with Washington as the customer.

nodes.t: Boreal East, building for the Union
nodes.x: Montreal's half of Boreal builds its own Muskeg successor on Union fuel cells and names it after the snowy owl. The Wapiti and the Harfang still share a chassis and a supplier list, although the two plants have had very little to say to each other for a century.

nodes.t: An ice and ocean frame for the Quebec fields
nodes.x: Boreal East's frame for the Union's hydrogen fields and the Arctic shelf: amphibious, ice-breaking and built to work under the sea ice where the pipelines run.

nodes.t: The Iron Ox goes back to digging
nodes.x: Tianlong's civil frame for China's aid missions: the Tieniu's excavator heritage rebuilt for construction, with a Tianshu link that schedules its work. It rebuilds Australia's towns and Córdoba's grid, and the protests in Córdoba are about its scheduler, not its shovel.

nodes.t: “Blizzard”: the steppe frame of the peace
nodes.x: Khiimori's post-war frame, built in the Darkhan sheds for the outriders under Beijing's protection: the Tsagaan Salkhi's speed in a frame at a price herders can actually pay.

nodes.t: Steppe riders in vacuum
nodes.x: The Steppe crews who went up to the Belt took Khiimori with them. The Saddle-S is a sealed Shuurga built for the Syndicate's Steppe-crewed ships, and its pilots fly it the way their ancestors rode.

nodes.t: Fission frames, kept off Earth
nodes.x: The Ascendancy keeps its fission frames past the Moon, where the Mandate does not reach. The Burya-K guards its Mercury holdings and its Venus stations. It never refuels, and it has never been inspected.

nodes.t: The Staya's heir, for oath-sworn pilots
nodes.x: OKB-7's frame for the Ascendancy's oath-sworn pilots after the Martian crisis: a knight's frame in the line of the Staya's Volks, on diesel at home and on fission off-world.

nodes.t: “Elephant”: a monsoon heavy for the Indian coast
nodes.x: Nashik Works' first frame of the peace, built for the coasts the monsoon raiders once hit: a heavy frame for flood and storm work as much as war, on twin diesels.

nodes.t: Paired frames for the oath-sworn who stayed
nodes.x: The Ashvins left for Jupiter, and Nashik went on building pairs for the pilots who stayed. The Simha is a sworn pair's frame for the Ascendancy, and the Ashva Compact, which remembers where its own frames came from, counts it as a cousin.

nodes.t: Rescue frames again, for Kansai
nodes.x: Under Beijing's protection, Mitsurugi revives the frame it began with: an unarmed rescue frame for Japan's earthquakes and floods. Kansai's civil defence flies them, and its protesters hum the old Kizuna's servo tune.

nodes.t: Raijin's partner, a century late
nodes.x: Mitsurugi's frame for Beijing's Belt patrols, built around Osaka's capacitors and named for the wind god who stands beside Raijin. Its engineers say it is the frame the Raijin should have been.

nodes.t: The Commonwealth's frame for a crowded world
nodes.x: Khartoum's frame for the 2320s: the Khamaseen's desert turbine with Harmattan-style shelter bays. It is built for a South America and a Middle East where every power wants influence and, for now at least, none of them wants a war.

nodes.t: The Elissa's heir, from a Tunis no longer European
nodes.x: With Tunis returned to the Commonwealth, the Tunis Works builds the Elissa's successor for the Charter. People there describe it as a medic's frame with a fighting arm, and it runs on the hydrogen trade.

nodes.t: Built in the leased port, for the Union
nodes.x: Under the 99-year lease, the Union keeps its port in Tunis and builds Bastides there for its southern fleet. Tunisian engineers build both the Commonwealth's Dido and the Union's Bastide-T, sometimes on the same shift.

nodes.t: Firebreaks for a healing planet
nodes.x: The Albedo's line continued: a frame for the reconstruction's reforestation crews, firefighters and flood teams. With the drought over and money pouring down from space, the UNEL plants forests with it.

nodes.t: The Observer, armoured this time
nodes.x: Shackleton Works' frame for 2327: an observer frame with armour, because the UNEL learned at Mars that witnesses get shot at.

nodes.t: The Grapnel's successor, built under the Second Seal
nodes.x: The UNEL's space frame after the Martian civil war, licensed to every navy that signed the Weapons Resolution and refused to the rest.

supers.label: Supers
supers.intro: Super robots appear in Gen 3, each a different answer to one question: what can the human spirit be made to do? Only the ███████ line comes from ███ ████████. The rest are human work: heretical science, latent spirit, or technology pushed further than it should go.
turns: Ascension's Ares mission brought back ████ ████ █████. Outside ███████ ████, almost nobody knows.
