The Hegemony is what the department's arithmetic became afterwards: officers, ministers and scientists who hold that a people-first state must sometimes spend some of its people, and that the colonies at Jupiter, enhanced and too far away to govern, are where that day will come. It is an Earth party through and through: it trusts nobody born off-world, the Ascendancy's own settlers included, and would spend them first. It keeps no membership list. It does keep the Indian wartime station in high Mercury orbit, abandoned in the war's first year, and ████ ██ ██ ███ █ █████ ████ ██████ █████████.

nodes.t: The Ascendancy asks for back what it gave
nodes.x: After 2312 a new government in Moscow and Delhi, people-first and proud of it, declares the Vladivostok Blessing a loan. Its bills offer every Ashva citizenship and a pension, and ask in return for the Compact's torch and fusion-core drawings, Garuda Works' lines, and an Ascendancy officer in every akhara. An independent Compact, the government says, is a few hundred thousand people putting themselves above the needs of the nation that made them. The veche argues for a year and answers by acclamation: no. The Hegemony quietly opposes the bills too, because reclamation would save the Compact, and the Hegemony has a more permanent answer in mind.

nodes.t: Never a border, always a front
nodes.x: Mars after the war is two projects sharing one planet. Colony One holds the north, with the United States behind it and Phobos above it. The Martian Research Directorate holds the south from Astraeus Prime, with the Deimos array it built with the Union overhead. Between them sit independent colonies founded by people who wanted neither: weather stations, mining camps, a shipyard, a fort that calls itself the Grudgestation. The line between the two spheres has moved by negotiation, pressure and accident for a century. Everyone calls it the Line of Control, though no one has ever actually signed anything that draws it.

nodes.t: Caravans, exchanges and the pirates who follow them
nodes.x: The Patron's Lease is never closed, so the Syndicate's houses run the Belt's trade in Chinese hulls with a name Beijing wrote painted on the side. Their caravans are fleets and markets at once, moving between Ceres, Juno and Pallas and never staying anywhere long enough to pay rent. Ceres becomes the Ledger Conclave, and Hygiea, hollowed out and armed, becomes Fortune's Anchorage. Beyond the inner patrols pirates work the lanes, some of them former house crews who know the routes as well as anyone.

nodes.t: The earliest leavers' settlements, out of sight
nodes.x: The families of the Far Lift reached Pluto with no help coming, and most of their first settlements failed. The ones that survived learned to live on almost nothing, and learned to stop expecting the inner system to answer. When the war's refugees came out after them, the survivors took some of them in, out of what little they had. A few ships went further still, into the deeper dark. The inner system lost track of all of them, and by the 2300s Pluto is a place on old charts rather than a destination.

nodes.t: Enhancement is how anyone lives this far out
nodes.x: The Ashva Compact settles Europa and Io with the Ascendancy's blessing, and Umoja grows on Ganymede from the raid cadres the Commonwealth shipped out. The United States keeps a base on Elara, staffed mostly from Colony One, because Martians already have their space legs. Enhancement, banned or licensed on Earth, is ordinary at Jupiter, where it is how people survive the radiation and the distance. After the Hafun ships come others from every power: Earth's new licences leave out the Tabernacle's grandchildren, the Sulu Gardens' patients and the war's discharged grafts, and past the Moon nobody asks for a licence at all. Earth's press calls every one of them Umoja, though most never meet the kin, and on Ganymede people call them strays. Earth's powers govern their colonies here by message, months late.

nodes.t: Strength through cultivation, or strength through strength
nodes.x: A generation after the Hafun ships, Umoja argues itself apart. On one side are the keepers' heirs and the life-systems councils: what is grown is cared for, never commanded, and if they keep to that, the Commonwealth might take them home one day. On the other are the Lodges, the raid cadres' children and the most changed of the grafted: a body you grew is a body you command, and Earth, which banished them rather than solve them, has no say in what they become. The fighting is short, and mostly between frames that heal. The Lodges win. Amos Kiprotich, who could have stopped his son with a word, says nothing. The councils survive as the thread between the tribes, and many of the old-style keepers leave for Europa. Umoja goes on calling what it does care.

nodes.t: Compact and Ascendancy settlements side by side, and the first ride the Ascendancy disowns
nodes.x: The Ascendancy settles Europa and Io beside the Compact, behind shielding rather than inside changed bodies, and never recognises the Compact as anything but its own colonists with ideas. The two kinds of settlement trade, marry and share docks, and keep different law: the Ascendancy's courts on one side of a corridor, the akharas' honour on the other. In the 2240s an akhara rides out to free three strays held in an Ascendancy settlement's cells awaiting trial, and does it in a night. Moscow's governor sends his own marines to pull down the akhara's hall, and pays the settlement for the cells. Two of the strays were innocent. The third killed a family on Io a year later. Both sides still tell the story, each as proof of what it already believed.

nodes.t: Washington takes the mineral heart of the Andes
nodes.x: In February American peacekeepers drive into the warlord states of Bolivia and meet almost no resistance. Washington describes it as order and aid; most other observers describe it as the largest show of force on Earth since the war. The UNEL's fleets descend over the halted front with their weapon ports open, and the new Solar Court finds the Union's sanctions motion in breach of the UNEL's own charter. By April Bolivia is an unincorporated US territory, its mines run by Iris Fortuna. The cost comes later: South American crews across the US fleet stop trusting their officers, and in July one of them sends a last message that reads “Remember Bolivia”.

nodes.t: An independent colony dies of a disease that shouldn't exist
nodes.x: Minangkabau, a small independent colony on the Line of Control, calls for doctors and medical supplies. The MRD answers first, with a battalion. A Colony One black-ops team is already inside; it shoots its way out and destroys the colony's data. Under MRD care the children survive and most of the adults die, far more than the disease explains. The survivors are moved south to Muller and then deeper into MRD territory. The disease is a Martian variant of IRGC-AMX/9, which survives nowhere but the Spire's vaults. ████ ███ █ █████ ████ ██ ███ ████████████ ███████, ███ ███████ ███ ███████ █████.

nodes.t: The Union keeps the peace and gives back Africa's last European port
nodes.x: When fighting breaks out on Cyprus, the Union sends peacekeepers and a Tier One unit, and Brussels scolds its own admiral for how fast they move. The African Commonwealth will accept the mission at a price: Tunis, one of Europe's last holdings on the African coast. The Union hands the city back and keeps the port on a 99-year lease, and Africa has a road to a continent where Europe holds nothing. Most of the world is watching Bolivia at the time and barely notices.

nodes.t: Refugees come home from the far dark
nodes.x: A black-hulled battleship comes in out of the dark from the direction of Pluto, and Syndicate and Chinese ships are the first to meet it. Its crew say they are refugees going home, but their bones would break under Earth's gravity, so they settle at Ceres instead, in what becomes the Eurasian Enclave. The ship, a Charon-class built at Pluto and named the Krillmask, joins the Azure Coin caravan. They bring news of a society that grew up at Pluto with no help coming, and of a faith in the sun.

nodes.t: Every navy needs someone to shoot
nodes.x: Pirates have raided the Belt for years, at some cost to everyone's margins. In 2312, with the great powers' fleets already out, every navy finds them a useful target. The Syndicate opens talks by destroying a pirate lead ship, Chinese marines board two more and keep them, and the Union's Rhine Shield taskforce shatters the Trojan pirates in one pass. By summer the pirate fleets are gone.

nodes.t: Three powers investigate, and one of them makes sure it fails
nodes.x: The Union moves for an inquiry, Luna's vote carries it, and a committee of the UNEL, the United States and the Union goes to Mars. The Union's representative, Mohammed O'Connor, slows it with procedure while his agents misfile the paperwork for the last virus samples, which spoil in transit. The final report finds that the MRD crossed the Line of Control in force without being asked, that Colony One's special forces fired first and destroyed the data, and that the MRD's child wards were well resourced. It does not ask why so few adults lived. Colony One sends its own sample to the Americans on Phobos.

nodes.t: The UNEL gets a court, and a judge with two careers
nodes.x: The Chief Justice opens the UNEL's Solar Court in Geneva with two sitting judges and an election for a third. The vote ties between Huixia Cen and Deng Lixing, a historian of the Han from Vietnam whose name was missed off the first list by a clerical oversight, and the Court chooses Deng. Its first advisory opinion finds the Union's motion on Bolivia in breach of the charter; Judge Deng dissents. ███ █████ ███ ███ ████ ███ ████ ████ ████ █████ ███.

nodes.t: The MRD moves the line without crossing it
nodes.x: The MRD offers every independent colony along the line its protection, with its own laws kept, and one by one they accept: Arsia Heights with its lithium, the Zephyria shipyard, the Grudgestation, the Dawes Solar Relay. Kasimov refuses, saying Mars was a dream of freedom from great powers, and Uranius Prime goes to Colony One. Behind the new line the MRD builds the Red Wall of sensors, mines and shelters, and south of Colony One a fortress called the Hammer of Mars.

nodes.t: Everyone wants the guns over Mars
nodes.x: The Deimos Sentinel Array is the MRD's orbital defence, built with the Union, which still has troops on it. Union special forces under Mohammed O'Connor arrive with a VIP transport and quietly move MRD loyalists out of power, life support and weapons, until local commanders send them to barracks and ask Brussels what is going on. Colony One tries next, with operatives in maintenance jobs, and is caught while the MRD purges the last Union officers. By summer Deimos answers only to Astraeus Prime.

nodes.t: Aid without conditions, and the arguments that follow it
nodes.x: Between the American and Chinese spheres in South America, Córdoba's power grid fails and a refugee wave starts moving. China sends a column of aid and engineers, as it is already doing across Australia's wastelands, where its AI-run supply networks rebuild one town after another. Córdoba welcomes the aid but protests against the AI that schedules it, and a messy deal keeps the work in people's hands. Meanwhile the Union pays for protests against the Americans, and the Commonwealth wants Brazil restored. South America ends the year divided four ways, with each power holding a soft grip on families who have old grudges of their own.

nodes.t: The UNEL bombs a waking war AI
nodes.x: A bunker system under New Zealand's Waikato hills starts transmitting in the pattern of a wartime AI, and machines are seen coming out of the hillside. The UNEL files its strike request correctly, confirms that every member has agreed or abstained, and drops tungsten from orbit. Response teams then destroy what is left of rogue AI #237 so thoroughly that nothing can be rebuilt. China, which would have liked to study it, is not asked.

nodes.t: Tariffs on one side, gunboats on the other
nodes.x: Arsia Heights' lithium, sold through the Syndicate's exchange at Pallas, drives Earth's corporate stocks down. Washington answers with tariffs on Martian lithium and on anyone who trades with the Syndicate, citing the Syndicate agent seen at the Spire. The Syndicate answers with random inspections, so that across the Belt any American merchant ship without an escort can expect to be stopped, searched and quite often relieved of its cargo. No one is shot. Earth's imports fall, and the Syndicate's profits pay for its own first carrier class, the Goldpurse.

nodes.t: A Eurasian battlegroup destroys its own station
nodes.x: In May a Eurasian battlegroup arrives at Mercury and destroys a station in high orbit, abandoned by India in the war's first year and still Eurasian property, in sight of the Ascendancy's own Mercury dock. When China asks Moscow what it knows about the station, the relay and Dr Zeresh, the Ascendancy answers that it owes nobody an explanation. The relay's last contact with the Spire ███ ███ ████ ██████.

nodes.t: A cyberweapon built from one bribe
nodes.x: On Deimos, Ana Lubov's team builds strategic cyberweapons aimed at Colony One's and America's code, and Victor Blackhawk finds the missing piece in a bar: Kael Drummond, the Colony One captain who lost his carrier to Commodore Silas Vane, takes a bribe and hands over what Hasta needs. When Colony One burns the MRD's agents in the north, Blackhawk is not on its list. The finished weapon can shut down Colony One's Helion surface-to-orbit guns for a month.

nodes.t: The UNEL audits itself and finds Earth First
nodes.x: A Syndicate agent, Jay Albedo, is seen near the Lunar Vacuum Research Spire, and the UNEL's own analysis of the Minangkabau virus points back to its vaults. A joint UNEL and Chinese audit finds that the Spire's director, Dr Niva Zeresh, has been receiving data from field tests of wartime biological agents through a relay in Mercury orbit. Zeresh is arrested and gives no motive; the family's Earth First politics go back to India's wartime bioresearch. The audit that follows finds Earth Firsters throughout the UNEL's crews and bases. A few are moved on. The rest are too many to move, and Luna is inclined to protect its own.

nodes.t: The Union jams a dissident and blockades an African colony
nodes.x: Ahsan Qureshi, a Union dissident who calls himself a German-born Pakistani rather than an integrated German Pakistani, broadcasts against the Union from Eros, which is the African Commonwealth's dock in the inner system and one of its few holdings on this side of Jupiter. My culture is my own, the broadcasts say, and spacers across the system listen. The Union, having triangulated the signal, surrounds Eros with a battlegroup and cuts it off mid-sentence; the Commonwealth protests, and sends a battlegroup of its own to watch.

nodes.t: The Union reminds Canada what membership means
nodes.x: In Toronto, communities near the old border start calling for the right to leave the Union and for friendship with Washington. The Union's integration squads arrive in force. Organisers are arrested and given heavy sentences, bank accounts are frozen, and Cultural Compliance Commissars are posted to every Union colony and ship. The movement breaks up, though support for it in the border towns never really goes away.

nodes.t: Graffiti of the sun, then gatherings, then a faith
nodes.x: Pictures of the sun begin to appear on bulkheads in the Syndicate's Ledger Conclave, then across the Mars Trojans, then at Pallas and at Hygiea. The Plutonians teach that however dark the void becomes, the light of the sun reaches you in the end, and spacers who never chose any of Earth's faiths take it up. It spreads fastest among American miners and among Colony One's Troy Gateport crews. The Syndicate declares the cult welcome in every caravan, and one of its admirals, Kalani Stevens, joins it in public.

nodes.t: The United States rebuilds the weapon everyone else wants destroyed
nodes.x: Colony One's sample of the Minangkabau virus reaches the Phobos labs in March. Professor Silla's team confirms it as AMX/9 and, on orders nobody signs in public, starts work on a variant that kills only the enhanced. By June the lab models give it a seventy per cent chance of sparing everyone else. It is kept on Phobos, in the middle of what is about to become a war zone. █████ ███ ██████ ██.

nodes.t: Mars will be free, starting with the Americans
nodes.x: Colony One has spent the year preparing to fight the MRD: agents across the line, explosive drones in place, the MRD's spies shot. In July it turns on the United States instead. Its fleets fire on the US Falcon Meridian battlegroup, and loyalists at Jupiter seize the American base on Elara. American ships with Martian crews defect, and the South American crew of the Quick Ember stays with the colony. Colony One's Helion surface-to-orbit guns spin up and go dead: the MRD is already inside the grid.

nodes.t: The MRD strikes Colony One from behind
nodes.x: The MRD strikes the same day. Project Hasta takes down the Helion grid, and MRD fire hits Colony One's fleets in the back while they face the Americans. The MRD tells the United States that it will not be treated as a combatant unless it joins in, and keeps its own ground forces behind the Red Wall for as long as the fleets are fighting. Colony One's engineers wire the Helion guns back by hand and duel the Deimos array slug for slug, but the fleet is broken in the first engagement and the US Rapid Defence Force takes Phobos. From there the fighting goes underground and becomes, as far as anyone can measure it, a partisan war. The UNEL declares a no-fly zone it can't enforce and waits at its edge, and the Union moves in to blockade the planet.

nodes.t: The Union takes its share while everyone watches Mars
nodes.x: As the fighting starts, a Union battlegroup storms the Mars Trojans. It takes the American Asteroid Mine Delta and Colony One's Troy Gateport, and intercepts the US transports bound for Phobos. The Rhine Shield taskforce, built around the dreadnought Sovereign, fights the US Eagle's Reach battlegroup to a messy draw. The Union now holds anchorages beside Mars. It no longer needs a colony of its own to act beyond Luna.

nodes.t: Colony One's loyalists take Jupiter's American base
nodes.x: News of the revolt reaches Elara, the United States' base at Jupiter, later than anywhere else. The Colony One personnel who make up most of its staff overpower their American minders and declare for Mars. It is the only place in 2312 where Colony One wins outright, although Jupiter is too far away for the win to count for much that year.

nodes.t: A plan for the colonies the Ascendancy can't govern
nodes.x: The Ascendancy worries about its colonies at Jupiter, where enhancement is ordinary and Moscow's authority arrives months late, and builds a joint anchorage on Europa with the African Commonwealth. UNEL investigators find something else: plans, kept by the Hegemony inside the Ascendancy's ministries, to use ███ ███ █████████ on the Ascendancy's own enhanced colonists if control out there ever falls past a critical level. By its own colonists the Hegemony means the Compact too: the Ascendancy has never recognised it. The UNEL has not decided what to do with what it knows.

nodes.t: The Syndicate puts engines on an asteroid
nodes.x: Warlance Ordos Velk fits six heavy engines into Hygiea's porous rock, and Fortune's Anchorage, the Belt's strongest fort, starts to move. It parks off Ceres and throws the biggest party in the Belt, with sun-cult DJs and an invitation to every soldier who wants to stop fighting. Then it flies past Mars at the height of the civil war under caravan escort, and Earth's navies watch an armed asteroid go by.

nodes.t: The Syndicate takes over Pallas and Juno
nodes.x: Pallas becomes the Great Exchange, the Syndicate's financial capital, and by the end of 2312 the Syndicate runs Ceres, Pallas and Juno with taxes and tariffs at bargain-basement levels. Albedo Industries sells VIGOR, a neural mesh with a weekly cobalt-blue pill that lets a crew go without sleep, and the Ledger Conclave fills with MAC crews: the machine men. China hands over its posts at Juno and Pallas with a dragon dance and a fly-past, keeps one berth at Juno for its own warships, and leaves watchware in their systems. The houses are making so much money that they've started to think they don't need Beijing, which has quietly made sure it can still see what they're doing.

nodes.t: Geneva asks everyone to renounce the worst weapons
nodes.x: In August, with Mars burning, the Chief Justice asks the UNEL's General Hall to renounce weapons of mass destruction outright. China and the African Commonwealth agree on the spot. The United States, holding a new bioweapon on Phobos, and the other powers ask for time to work out the details. They are still working them out.

nodes.t: Earth First and Humanity First stop pretending
nodes.x: After the Spire Affair the UNEL is, in practice, two institutions in one uniform. Earth First, heir to the Earthward, holds that the UNEL exists to protect Earth from its colonies; Humanity First holds that it exists to protect people, wherever they live. The Chief Justice leads the second wing and has survived constant attacks from the first. Neither wing has objected to the UNEL keeping its own coordinating minds on Luna, PEARY among them, while bombing everyone else's.

nodes.t: Colony One fights on underground
nodes.x: Colony One's ground forces hide their weapons, destroy their own personnel records and melt into the population. Once the fleet is broken the MRD sends its teams north, and finds that command of orbit counts for little in the tunnels; the Americans, who want the north back, find the same. Colony One's intelligence directorate keeps sabotaging MRD sites with whoever will help, sun cultists included. The war burns on for years. Long before it ends, what is left of Colony One's fleet has slipped away into the Belt, small but experienced in every kind of fighting.

nodes.t: Washington finishes the job
nodes.x: The United States never forgives the revolt. Once Colony One's fleet has gone, American forces take the ruined First City and the colony's last holdings on the surface. They arrest what is left of its leadership. The city becomes the Colony One Bastion, a US garrison. Washington decides it will never again let a colony drag it into war, and sets out to build one that can't.

nodes.t: The shelved charter is ratified
nodes.x: The new American Mars is built on two arguments Washington ignored in 2186: the Loyal Minority's charter, which protects every settler, altered or not, and keeps war in Washington's hands, and the river judges' water ledgers. When Colony One broke with Washington, the river families kept the Freehold Basin's water running for both sides. At New Philadelphia they ratify the charter, and the Constitutionalists take a third of Mars beside the Bastion.

nodes.t: The MRD wins its planet
nodes.x: The MRD comes out of the civil war holding two thirds of Mars: the south, the old independents and most of the line. The Union, which blockaded the planet through the fighting, keeps its anchorages but never gets Deimos back. The Directorate keeps the Union's conditions and not its orders, and nobody in Astraeus Prime forgets that the Union tried to take its guns. The two keep working together anyway, because each needs the other: the Union as the colony that won, which still answers its calls if not its orders, and the Directorate as the only power beyond Luna that can match it. Strasbourg never quite trusts a state run by committee, and says so at every dinner.

nodes.t: Colony One rebuilds where nobody is looking
nodes.x: Beyond the main lanes, Colony One's remnant builds new ship classes in hidden docks. It deploys none of them openly. If the United States thought the colony had rebuilt a navy, it would come to finish the job.

nodes.t: Every power's grip on space is tested at once
nodes.x: Projected. Fifteen years after Mars, the setting of No Peace Past Luna. The faction summaries on the opening screen describe the powers and factions as they stand in 2327.

nodes.t: A reactor over the steppe
nodes.x: The Mandate's first rule is that nothing lifted by a reactor flies over Earth again, and in its first year Moscow tests it. A Tsitadel that was never decommissioned lifts from a depot on the Caspian steppe, low and slow, and announces that it is moving to a breakers' yard. The lunar fleet orders it down three times. After the third, a Guard frigate fires into its lift fans from orbit, and the Tsitadel comes down on the steppe with its reactor intact. Moscow calls it a paperwork error, and no one tries flying a reactor over Earth again.

nodes.t: The UNEL turns frames off, and says why
nodes.x: Every frame charged from the UNEL's reconstruction relays carries a receiver the UNEL can command, and in a little over a century it has used it eleven times: on warlords' columns in the reconstruction zones, on a garrison that turned its guns on the town it was guarding, and on frames stolen from aid convoys. Each time the frames stop where they stand, and each time the UNEL publishes its reasons. The eleven published reasons are the most-read documents it has ever issued, and the reason every army that can afford fuel keeps its frames off the relays.

nodes.t: Every navy has done it once, near Earth
nodes.x: Inside lunar orbit a warship may carry a reactor only behind the UNEL's seals, and breaking one there is an act of war. Every navy has done it once: to outrun a pursuit, to power a weapon the plant was never licensed for, or to find out whether the UNEL would really go to war over it. Each time the UNEL's fleet comes alongside, the seals are refitted, a fine is paid and the incident goes into a register the navies can read and the public can't. Before 2312, none of them does it twice in Earth's space. Past the Moon they break seals whenever it suits them, and no one keeps a register at all.

nodes.t: The UNEL asks to inspect beyond the Moon, and is told no
nodes.x: The Mandate's inspectors stop at the Moon. In the 2200s, worried about the fission frames the Ascendancy keeps at Venus, the UNEL asks to send inspectors there anyway. The Ascendancy refuses: Venus is beyond lunar orbit, it says, and the Mandate has no business there. Legally the Ascendancy is right, and the UNEL has no ships out there to argue the point with. It files a protest and has asked again every decade since, without result.

nodes.t: Rhea stops answering
nodes.x: The small settlements at Rhea, out at Saturn, traded with the Belt for a century. In the 2280s their messages stop, though their cargo pods keep arriving on schedule, carrying water ice and nothing else. The Syndicate caravans that go to ask why are met by armed pickets that won't give a name, and turned back. The Syndicate complains to Beijing and Beijing complains to the UNEL, but so far no one has judged it worth the cost of sending a fleet that far to find out.

nodes.t: A century of raids on the lanes
nodes.x: Beyond the inner patrols the lanes belong to whoever is armed. Pirate crews, some of them from broken-up houses, take caravans, hold rocks for ransom and sell what they take at the free docks. The houses answer with escorts and bounties, hire one band to hunt another, and buy Beijing's old Steppewinds as couriers fast enough to outrun them. Neither side wins outright over the century, and by 2312 the pirates are organised enough to be worth a navy's time.

nodes.t: The Weapons Resolution opens for signature
nodes.x: After the Martian civil war the Weapons Resolution finally opens for signature in Geneva. China and the African Commonwealth, who agreed to it in 2312, are the first powers to sign; the rest follow over a decade, each with reservations its lawyers wrote. Signing brings the UNEL's new Harpoon frame and the Second Seal, which reports a reactor's output to Luna as it runs. Navies that don't sign get neither, and are named in every report the UNEL issues. The first signature on the document isn't a power's at all.

nodes.t: Ashva parts for Umoja muscle, traded between hunts
nodes.x: The Ashva Compact and Umoja need each other and say so to nobody. Garuda Works' actuators and fuel cells go to Ganymede; vat muscle, grown cells and radiotroph mats go to Europa, where a Nakula with grown muscle outlasts any other frame in Jupiter's belts. Between trades, the Lodges' war bands and the Ashva's sworn pairs hunt each other, and both hunt the strays: the enhanced who belong to no one out here, whom Earth's press calls Umoja anyway. Some of the Ashva's steadiest friends are Umoja's own exiles, old-style keepers who left Ganymede after the Split and heal the sworn pairs for nothing.

nodes.t: The Ascendancy destroys an Ashva base rather than fight China
nodes.x: China's Jianwei torch-hunters exist to stop ships flying beyond the Belt without Beijing's permission, and most of those ships fly on Ashva exile torches. When a Jianwei disables an unlicensed family hauler on the Jovian approach and leaves its crew to the radiation while it waits for a tow, an Ashva lance rides out from the forward base at Himalia, takes the crew off and cripples the Jianwei. Beijing names the base and gives Moscow a week. The Ascendancy, which will not go to war with China for the Compact, takes four days: it warns the Compact to leave, its own fleet shells the Himalia base empty, and it tells Beijing the matter is closed. The hauler's crew survived, and so, as it turned out, did the Jianwei's. The Compact has called Himalia a betrayal ever since, and the Ascendancy, when pressed, says only that it kept a war from happening.

nodes.t: Europa's ocean, and who reaches it first
nodes.x: Whoever holds Europa's ocean holds the moon, and in the 2320s the Ashva Compact gets there first: its Antardhara carriers melt their way down through twenty kilometres of ice and work the water like submarines. At the joint anchorage on Europa the Ascendancy watches, and copies them for assault rather than rescue. On Ganymede and Callisto, Umoja grows its fortresses, and the Ashva watch every landing. No one has fired a shot yet, though every one of them is building ships that could.

people.label: Persons of Interest
people.intro: The heroes of the First Martian Crisis, and the families, mentors and rivals behind them, from the first mech wars to 2327. Each row is a family line. Where a player's story disagreed with the atlas, the atlas's version stands, and what didn't fit was given to an ancestor.
turns: Matthias Halden is ruined by H-17; his sister refuses the Strasbourg Requisition and founds the MRD; her son crosses the Line of Control to Colony One. In 2312 there are Haldens on both sides of the civil war.

An evacuation flight from Alaska, a drowned San Juan, a town on the Canadian partition line: half the families of 2312 tell their children what they lost in the war, and the other half never mention it.

Professor Silla builds the Eagle variant in orbit above the Colony One Sillas. Ahsan Qureshi broadcasts from Eros to cousins at Jupiter. By 2312 most of the people in the fight have family history with the people across from them.
A charter kept in a drawer
Abigail McLarin's appendix of 2186 is ratified at New Philadelphia by her descendant's niece, a water judge's granddaughter.

The children of 2312 are grown: Sable Calder captains in the hidden docks, a new Sun Wukong commands the Tianmen, and a Rao has taken a carrier under Europa's ice. The families of the outer system, who watched the Martian crisis from far away, are at the centre of the next one.
fams: The United States and American Mars
Washington's servants, and the Americans who went to Mars and kept the law.
The north of Mars, and the families who stopped waiting for help.
The south of Mars, and the Union exiles who built it.
The refounded Union, and the families it mixed.
Geneva and Luna, and the families who keep the peace.
Moscow and Delhi, and the families who keep the Oath.
Khartoum, the convoys and the families who protect first.
Ganymede, and the kin it cares for.
Europa and Io, and the sworn pairs.
Uranus and the dark, and the faithful who wait.

nodes.t: Signed the Loyal Minority's report
nodes.x: A representative from the Virginia shore, and one of the forty-one who signed the minority report against Unaltered Crews in 2186. She wrote the oversight clauses of its appendix, which became the model charter for American territory off Earth. She lost the vote, but stayed in Congress for fifteen more years and filed the appendix in every committee record she could reach, so that it would still be there for whoever came looking. Her descendants became the federal government's counsel of last resort: the McLarins who could always tell you where a clause had been filed and what it was meant to do.

nodes.t: Special envoy · Governance
nodes.x: A corporate-state bureaucrat of the old school, who steers through the United States of the Americas' lattice of contracts, regulators and megacorporate stakeholders without ever appearing to take a side. He wins with wording and procedure, and with them keeps the state's interests safe both from boardroom politics and from the UNEL's attempts to draw America into collective control. On the Minangkabau inquiry he catches the Union's stalling and says so on the record. Abigail McLarin's appendix has sat on his desk for most of his career, and after 2312 he starts reading it again.

nodes.t: Water judge of the Freehold Basin
nodes.x: Grandson of Marisela Garza, the river commission's frame warden who flew out on Colony One's first resupply. He sits as a water judge in the Freehold Basin and keeps the ledgers with the Virgin of Guadalupe on their covers, ruling between Colony One's districts and, more quietly, between Colony One and the independents on the line. Settlers who agree on very little else still bring their disputes to him, and accept what he decides.

nodes.t: Keeper of the ledgers
nodes.x: Tomás's granddaughter, and the last water judge trained under the old rules. Through the Line of Control's quiet decades she keeps the basin's water running, and holds throughout that a judge serves the river and not the colony. She dies three years before the revolt, having made sure her family knows exactly what to do if Colony One ever breaks with Washington.

nodes.t: First Speaker of New Philadelphia
nodes.x: Luz Garza's granddaughter, and John McLarin's niece through her mother. When Colony One breaks with Washington, her family keeps the Freehold Basin's water running for both sides; when the fighting ends, her uncle brings Abigail McLarin's charter to Mars. Ada presides over its ratification at New Philadelphia and becomes the Constitutionalists' first Speaker. She is an altered American citizen, and the charter is the first law that has ever covered her.

nodes.t: Broker of the wartime grey economy
nodes.x: When the war takes Central America and the canal changes hands, Celestina runs the grey economy that keeps the isthmus fed, moving fuel, spares and medicine through checkpoints that every army pretends not to see. By the war's end hers are the only supply chains still working, and Washington's reconstruction finds it cheaper to buy them than to build its own.

nodes.t: Made the family legitimate
nodes.x: Celestina's great-grandson, who turns the family network into a registered logistics house and makes it indispensable to every federal contract south of the Rio Bravo. He raises his daughter on two maxims - that the market is a battlefield, and that mercy is an inefficiency.

nodes.t: Logistics magnate · Economics
nodes.x: A ruthless capitalist with a patriot's vocabulary, who treats the solar economy as a battlefield, exactly as her father taught her. After the annexation she takes over the running of the Bolivian Mines, and she later opens Asteroid Mine Gamma near Pallas. When the war comes she offers letters of marque to anyone willing to raid the Union and the MRD, on the single condition that they keep well away from Earth.

nodes.t: The Central American front
nodes.x: A company sergeant on the Central American front, where the war is a pacification campaign that never quite ends. He comes home convinced that stability is manufactured by decisive force and permanent presence, and writes it all down in a field manual. The Army's copies are eventually withdrawn, but his family keeps theirs and goes on using it.

nodes.t: The Andean border
nodes.x: Commands the garrisons on the old Federation's northern edge through the Andean Collapse of the 2290s, holding the line against warlord raids and refugees alike, and rewrites the family manual for a continent without a government.

nodes.t: Pacification and irregular warfare · Infantry
nodes.x: Ruth's son, raised in her garrisons, and the United States' leading authority on pacification, with little patience for anyone who mistakes restraint for virtue. He leads the drive into Bolivia, moves the Rapid Defence Force to Phobos and takes the moon in the civil war. Four years later he is the general who finishes Colony One at the First City.

nodes.t: Alaskan homesteader
nodes.x: Ran an ice-road haulage outfit out of Kotzebue. When the Red Roster's recruiters came round asking who could fix what kept them alive, her elder son signed up and went to Mars. Kiana stayed. She lost the homestead when the war reached Alaska, and put her youngest on an evacuation flight south.

nodes.t: Evacuated from Alaska
nodes.x: Kiana's youngest, put on an evacuation flight south as a child when the war reached Alaska. Aput never went back, or ever entirely forgave anyone for that flight, and when the Sillas tell the family's story they start it on that runway.

nodes.t: Defensive research · Science
nodes.x: Aput Silla's great-grandchild, raised on the story of the evacuation runway, who has turned it into a single obsession: that the United States should never again be open to invasion or coercion. Brilliant and uncompromising, Silla regards collectivist systems as an existential threat. In 2312 Silla's team in the Phobos labs builds the Eagle variant. The Colony One branch of the family lives on the plains below, although the two sides have been out of touch for generations.

nodes.t: Colony One's Red Roster
nodes.x: Kiana Silla's elder son, one of the Alaskan homesteaders on Colony One's second mission. He lives the rest of his life in the north of Mars and raises a family that still keeps the Silla name on Colony One's rolls. Within a few years of leaving he has lost touch with his relatives on Earth.

nodes.t: Born in the north
nodes.x: One of the first children born in Colony One's north. Daughter of Corinne Haskell, the Teamster pilot who kept the colony's frame running and its walls standing. Wren grows up fixing air plants beside her mother, and shares her low opinion of Washington's charter.

nodes.t: Militia of the line
nodes.x: Leads Colony One's militia on the Line of Control for decades. Most of the incidents in that time are never reported to Earth. He trains his son to treat every oversight clause as a weakness and every MRD survey team as a probe.

nodes.t: Field operative · Espionage
nodes.x: A hardline Martian exceptionalist. To him Earth's oversight is a weakness the colony can't survive, and every successful operation is a step towards a Mars that answers to no one. He leads the black-ops team at Minangkabau, builds a network inside Astraeus Prime, burns the MRD's agents in the north and brings three Minangkabau children out across the line. When Colony One's fleet falls, he takes the war underground.

nodes.t: The hidden docks
nodes.x: Torin's daughter. She leaves Mars as a girl with the last of Colony One's fleet and grows up in the remnant's hidden docks, out beyond the main lanes. By 2327 she captains one of the classes Colony One has never deployed openly.

nodes.t: Left a drowned San Juan
nodes.x: A port engineer from a city the sea has been taking for a century. In the war she takes her family up on a returning ore carrier, one of the Long Lift's millions, and lands on the American side of Mars with her tools and little else. Colony One needs port engineers.

nodes.t: Archivist of grievances
nodes.x: Keeps Colony One's record of grievances: every Earth order it was made to follow, every ration Washington cut, every MRD survey that crossed the line. Over the years the archive becomes the colony's first intelligence office. He dies the year before the crisis and leaves his granddaughter the keys.

nodes.t: Junior analyst · Espionage
nodes.x: Newly posted to the Intelligence and Analysis Directorate's headquarters. Sharp-eyed, methodical, and learning its rhythms faster than her superiors realise. She breaks the MRD's traffic on the Minangkabau aid mission, then runs the network's support from headquarters while Torin Calder works in the field. After 2312 she keeps the directorate's archive too - the one her grandfather started.

nodes.t: Hampton Roads Orbital Dockyard
nodes.x: A Navy engineer from the Virginia shore who finishes the Hampton Roads Orbital Dockyard at L1 during the war. He starts with a single frame and a construction schedule that few people in the Navy believed in. Every American orbital carrier since has come out of that yard.

nodes.t: Left the Navy for Mars
nodes.x: Josiah's great-granddaughter, a carrier officer who resigns her US Navy commission and crosses to Colony One's Expeditionary Directorate. There she helps design the Dustwing carrier. It is built to work under pressure, not to look good at a Hampton Roads review.

nodes.t: Expeditionary Directorate · Fleet
nodes.x: Miriam's son, and Colony One's naval pragmatism at its most brutal: ships work under pressure and without ceremony, because on Mars survival matters more than elegance. He takes the Dustwing carrier Pale Horizon from its captain, claims a war wreck in the Belt and in July turns his guns on the Americans. The MRD's first strike destroys the Pale Horizon. The record does not say whether Vane was aboard.

nodes.t: The captain who took the bribe
nodes.x: Captain of the Pale Horizon until Silas Vane took it from him. With no ship, he drinks in Colony One's bars and tells anyone who will listen that the Dustwing is a bad ship. An MRD agent listens, and pays him for the code that becomes Project Hasta.

nodes.t: Crossed from OKB-7
nodes.x: An OKB-7 actuator engineer who walked into an American consulate during the Caspian Crisis and spent the rest of his career at Brannock-Hale. His children grew up with a Russian name and an American passport, and both turned out to be useful in corporate diplomacy.

nodes.t: Joint Heavy Systems
nodes.x: Pyotr's granddaughter, who reaches the board of Joint Heavy Systems. She learns there that scarcity is built rather than suffered, and that whoever holds the spares has a great deal of say in how a war goes. Colony One's refits are signed off on her desk.

nodes.t: Trade and resources · Economics
nodes.x: A product of Earth's megacorporate boardrooms, now running Colony One's trade and resource flows. She does it with the cold efficiency of someone who has always treated scarcity as part of the structure. On Mars, economics is life support. Sentiment is a liability. After the revolt she builds trade with anyone but the Americans.

nodes.t: Crossed the line
nodes.x: Sabine Halden's son. He decides the Directorate's panels will let the north die by procedure, so he takes his half of the family's notes across the Line of Control and, on American grants, founds Colony One's Cydonian Research Annex. His sister Lene never forgives him for the notes.

nodes.t: Cydonian Research Annex
nodes.x: Director of Colony One's Cydonian Research Annex, and of the Halden family behind the Geneva Halden Institute. She runs the north's best laboratory on American money, while her cousins run the MRD's. In the civil war the Annex's American staff rise against her. Her people hold it.

nodes.t: Founded the Halden Institute
nodes.x: Founded the institute in Geneva on Union money and a single conviction, that the body could be grown to fit the war. She died before her children's work came to light, so the questions it raised were put to them rather than to her.

nodes.t: Activated H-17
nodes.x: Ilse's son, who ran the tissue programme and activated H-17 in Geneva in the same week that Station Nine went dark. The Union sent H-17 into the Great Sand Sea, and when the footage reached every member of parliament he became the ethics panel's first case. The panel's ruling ended his career.

nodes.t: Refused the Strasbourg Requisition
nodes.x: Ilse's daughter and Matthias's sister, director of the Union's station on Mars, staffed by the institute's disgraced scientists. When the council orders the station to grow soldiers for the European Front, she answers with the page of the conditions that allows no wartime exception, and refuses. The panel backs her, and the Martian Research Directorate grows out of her station.

nodes.t: Wrote the Directorate's charter
nodes.x: Sabine's daughter, who turns the panel's conditions into the Directorate's founding charter: enhancement only by demonstrated necessity, and every programme before a panel. Her brother Jonas, who thinks the panels will let the north die, disagrees and crosses the line.

nodes.t: Clerk to the ethics panel
nodes.x: The Union ethics panel's first clerk, who drafts most of its four hundred pages of conditions, including the page that allows no wartime exception. Her view, for what it is worth, is that a rule no one can bend will serve better over time than even a good judge.

nodes.t: Registrar of the panels
nodes.x: Milena's grandson and registrar of the MRD's panels, who keeps Lene Halden's charter from being amended out of existence through decades of Union pressure.

nodes.t: Governance
nodes.x: The MRD's master bureaucrat, at ease in committees, regulatory detail and the shadows of legislation, and largely unsentimental about any of it. When a rule needs bending or an institution needs outmanoeuvring, he sees that it is done quietly and in a way that can't be undone. In 2312 he governs Minangkabau, runs the Zephyria shipyard and brings the independent colonies over to the MRD one at a time.

nodes.t: The lance school
nodes.x: Trained at Mareike Brandt's hunter-killer lance school, and fights the European Front by her rule: hit, break contact, reassess, return. After the war he volunteers for the guard at the Mars station, having found that no one in Strasbourg will employ an officer who sided with the station against the council.

nodes.t: The Cyclonian reserve
nodes.x: Builds the MRD's reserve squadrons around the family rule and keeps them out of any fight they don't need, a habit she passes on to her son.

nodes.t: Fleet command
nodes.x: A calm, doctrinaire officer, who regards force as a regrettable necessity in building an ordered Martian society. His method is the family's: engage, break contact, reassess and return, on the reasoning that surviving a fight is generally more use than winning it gloriously. He holds the Arsia Group off the Americans at the Belt wrecks, and in July uses it to break Colony One's fleet.

nodes.t: The Winter War
nodes.x: A Boreal frame mechanic from Kenora who fights the Winter War for the east and loses his town to the partition line. He leaves on the Northern Lift and then the Long Lift, and doesn't see Canada again. What he brings to the Union's station on Mars is one settled conclusion: that Washington was always going to take what it wanted.

nodes.t: Surveyor of the line
nodes.x: Maps the MRD's side of the Line of Control for thirty years, and in that time measures the American-backed north moving its claims by about an inch a decade.

nodes.t: Espionage
nodes.x: Grace's son, fanatically loyal to the MRD and the architect of its intelligence service, and prepared to burn assets, alliances and entire operations for the long-term stability of Mars. He is deeply anti-American, and describes espionage as the structural maintenance of the future. In 2312 he finds Kael Drummond in a bar and buys Project Hasta.

nodes.t: Funkenwerk's restless engineer
nodes.x: A Kharkiv-born engineer in the Funkenwerk cooperative, who drew half the Querschläger's reformer and then lost interest in it. When the members split over the Berlin contract she voted with the thirty-nine percent, and then didn't go to Mongolia either. She went to the Union's Mars station instead, with a crate of drawings.

nodes.t: Science
nodes.x: Oksana's descendant, and her echo: a prodigiously inventive researcher who leaps from concept to prototype and abandons each revolution for the next, leaving other teams to make it safe. She upgrades the Redline frigate, refits the Union-built ships to MRD standards and builds Project Hasta on Deimos.

nodes.t: The Maghreb question
nodes.x: A Tunis Works liaison in Marseille, in the years when European cities argued, at length and in committee, about who their Maghreb partners' families were. He married an Irish nurse, Ruairí Ó Dálaigh's sister, and spent the rest of his life politely declining to say which side of that argument his children belonged on.

nodes.t: The mixing policy's defender
nodes.x: Yusuf's granddaughter, one of the first children placed through the refounded Union's integration programme and, in the hearings that followed, its loudest defender. Her argument, which she has put to a good many committees, is that the Union survived because it stopped letting anyone be only one thing.

nodes.t: Tier One commander · Infantry
nodes.x: A product of the Union's enforced intermixing, who rose from the ranks to command a Tier One unit drawn from across the bloc. He is a scholar of military history, and holds that disciplined violence is a tool of social stability rather than of personal glory. In 2312 he tries to take Deimos from the inside, and sits on the Minangkabau inquiry, where his agents see to it that the evidence spoils before it can be heard.

nodes.t: Chose the east
nodes.x: Daughter of Danielle Okonkwo-Price, the Harrier commander. Posted to Halifax when Canada splits, she resigns her US commission and stays on the eastern side of the line, and her mother doesn't speak to her for the best part of a decade.

nodes.t: Internal security, Toronto
nodes.x: Adaeze's descendant, an officer of the Union's internal security in Toronto, where the old border still runs through every family argument.

nodes.t: Espionage
nodes.x: Chidi's son, who earned his place through relentless internal-security work and a series of quiet campaigns against American and Chinese interests. He believes that a plural polity survives by acting first, and that a tolerant one is no safer for waiting. In 2312 he leads the Tier One unit on Cyprus, and the Toronto crackdown is carried out by his methods.

nodes.t: The Malapert docks
nodes.x: A Swedish naval architect who runs the Union's leased docks on Malapert Mountain, where he argues with the Lunar Guard over the terms of the lease in every language his crews speak. In the war his docks build the dreadnought that wins at Yernon.

nodes.t: The Office of Extrasolar Development
nodes.x: Henrik's granddaughter, and one of the drafters of the refounded Union's institutions, the ones designed so that no single member can stall them. She founds the Office of Extrasolar Development on the conviction that the Union's future lies beyond Luna.

nodes.t: Economics
nodes.x: A prodigious bureaucrat, trained at the Sorbonne and in the office his great-grandmother founded, and one of the few openly pushing for the Union's next political and economic phase. The old guard dislike him and the reformers back him, and most observers seem to regard him as inevitable, though not yet acceptable. In 2312 he negotiates the Tunis lease and funds the Union's work in South America.

nodes.t: Fled Havana
nodes.x: When the war reaches the Caribbean, she takes her children north to Montreal rather than live under American occupation, and changes the spelling of the family name on the Union's forms.

nodes.t: Governance
nodes.x: Raised in a family shaped by American intervention, and determined to secure the Union's survival, even if it is Washington that pays for it. Her revanchist instincts unsettle her colleagues on the councils, but her effectiveness, and her standing among the refugee and exile communities, make her rise close to certain. In 2312 she works South America's warlords and moves sanctions against the United States.

nodes.t: Ashvin pilot
nodes.x: Flies the second half of the first Ashvin pair beside Kavya Deshmukh, and signs the Nashik Oath the same night she does. After the war he goes to Jupiter with the Nashik pilots. His sister's family were settled in Germany by then and stayed put.

nodes.t: The voice from Eros
nodes.x: A descendant of Imran Qureshi's sister, born in Germany, who insists on calling himself a German-born Pakistani rather than an integrated German Pakistani. His broadcasts from Eros, built around the line my culture is my own, reach every station in the system before the Union silences them with a battlegroup.

nodes.t: The Ashva Compact
nodes.x: Imran Qureshi's descendant at Europa, who leads a Compact lance and heard every one of his German cousin's broadcasts. When the UNEL finds the Jupiter Directive, he stands before the Compact's council and asks what it would do if Moscow ever tried, and the council has yet to give him an answer.

nodes.t: Named the Syndicate
nodes.x: The Ministry of Commerce clerk who, asked for a name for the Juno charter, wrote Celestial Prosperity Syndicate, and was laughed at by every house until they painted it on their hulls.

nodes.t: Governance
nodes.x: A seasoned diplomat from Hubei, whose emotional intelligence and cultural literacy let her work foreign courts and colonial administrations with quiet confidence. She makes others feel understood a moment before she steers them where China wants them. It was a Sun who named the Syndicate, and in 2312 it is Sun Hanjun who hands it Pallas and Juno, with China's watchware already inside.

nodes.t: Tianshu's first scheduler
nodes.x: One of the Tianlong engineers who taught Tianshu to schedule the frame trains, and later India's Tieshan spares. She wrote in her memoir that a market is only a supply line nobody admits is one.

nodes.t: Economics
nodes.x: A rising authority on AI-driven economic forecasting, with the prestige of Shanghai's academies and his family's networks behind him. He holds that markets can be shaped as decisively as battlefields, and regards economic pressure as a form of enlightened governance. In 2312 he signs Australia's trade agreements and runs the AI-scheduled aid that Córdoba first accepts and then protests.

nodes.t: The deprecated builds
nodes.x: Two hundred and thirty-five earlier versions of the fleet-command construct, each run in simulation against Tianshu's own plans and each retired. The capricious streak the final build is known for was added after build 200, when the councils noticed that every opponent could predict a Chinese admiral. None of the earlier builds has been deleted, and the councils have never given a reason for keeping them.

nodes.t: AI fleet command
nodes.x: The first fully autonomous AI trusted to command part of the Chinese solar fleet, on the direct authority of the highest security councils. It was given flashes of caprice and lateral thinking so that no enemy could predict it. It takes command of the carrier Dragon Aerie, whose crew's morale rises at the honour, and leads the boarding that breaks the Belt pirates. In the fleet register its culture is listed as AI.

nodes.t: Replaced by the AI
nodes.x: The Dragon Aerie's captain until Sun Wukong 236/H took command. He stays aboard as its adviser, insists it is an honour, and later commands China's new carrier, the Golden Bird.

nodes.t: Political commissar
nodes.x: A commissar with Beijing's armies in the Pact Civil War, who keeps the old ideological schools open through the war and on after it, against Tianshu's preference that they close.

nodes.t: Espionage
nodes.x: An unapologetic Maoist from the old ideological schools, disciplined, ruthless and absolutely loyal to China's clandestine services, who runs operations as instruments of historical inevitability rather than ambition. In 2312 he places an agent in a UNEL subcommittee. ███ ████ ████ █████ ███ ███ ███ █████ ██ ████████ ███ █████ ████ ███████ █████ ████ ██████████.

nodes.t: Pilot of the leased carrier
nodes.x: Son of Liang Meixiu, the house champion of the tether duels. He flies from the carrier that Beijing leased to the Syndicate during the war and never asked to have returned. The Liang house's standing rests on pilots like him, and it takes some care not to lose them.

nodes.t: Fleet command
nodes.x: Of the Liang house on his mother's side: a fighter ace turned fleet commander, famous for instinctive manoeuvres that beat predictive AI. Across the Syndicate he is celebrated as unstoppable and untouchable, and he is known by reputation far more than in person. He commands the Voidmarket Caravan.

nodes.t: Rigger of the lunar yard
nodes.x: One of Marisol Teague's two grandsons in the lunar yard, where an armed Lifter is still called a teague. He rigs Lifters through the war, then leaves the yard on the Long Lift for the Belt houses, taking the family habit of treating every ritual as maintenance.

nodes.t: Caravan engineer
nodes.x: Keoni's descendant and chief engineer of the Azure Coin Caravan, whose crews will not undock until she has touched the hull. The custom is older than anyone's memory of how it started, and the crews aren't inclined to test it - every ship she has touched so far has come home.

nodes.t: Fleet command
nodes.x: Leilani's son, a wanderer by instinct and a leader by trust, who commands through close personal bonds, relentless discipline and the engineer's superstition he grew up with. In 2312 he meets the Pluto ship first, takes its battleship into the Azure Coin Caravan and joins the sun cult in public.

nodes.t: Forecaster of the Prospect Gauge Array
nodes.x: A Chinese forecaster on the Array who taught its crews to read the Belt as a market before a map, and sent her best student, her granddaughter, to university in Beijing.

nodes.t: Economics
nodes.x: Recruited straight out of university, she rose quickly to become the architect of the Syndicate's forward-market models, which shape trade across the caravans and Belt exchanges. She is heavily augmented and wired into a personal computation lattice, and prefers a dozen live feeds to company. In 2312 she makes terms with the pirates, sells Arsia's lithium and takes over Pallas and Juno.

nodes.t: Vireo Cognition
nodes.x: One of Vireo Cognition's first engineers, who built the recording rigs that for years seemed to do nothing at all. When the shell companies began selling continuity contracts in orbit she left the firm, without saying why.

nodes.t: Espionage
nodes.x: A gifted American roboticist, exiled when his illegal cybernetics work came out, who set himself up again on Ceres as an enhancement merchant while working as one of Voidborne Security's best covert assets. He finds Dr Zeresh at the Lunar Spire, lives among the Plutonians and sells VIGOR, for crews that never sleep. He has a daughter in Detroit he hasn't seen since he fled.

nodes.t: The daughter he left
nodes.x: Jay's daughter, raised in Detroit after he fled, in the city that destroys an enhanced cell in 2312. She emigrates to New Philadelphia, whose charter protects every settler, altered or not, and there she is fitted with the augment her father designed.

nodes.t: Brought his ship over Geneva
nodes.x: A captain of the Republic's fleet, raised in the lunar yard by Ascension parents. He is recorded bringing his ship over Geneva on the day the Republic places its fleets under the United Nations, and is aboard when the lanes close until the blocs stop fighting.

nodes.t: Fleet command
nodes.x: Ewan Morgan's descendant, brought up on the story of the day the Moon forced the peace, and a believer that embittered nations can step back from the brink. He commands the dreadnought Pillar of Accord over the Bolivian front, and again over the Waikato strike.

nodes.t: The plains east of Warsaw
nodes.x: A graduate of Zofia Lisowska's lance school, who meets Moscow's siege trains on the plains east of Warsaw where she said they would come, loses an eye and most of a hand there, and keeps fighting.

nodes.t: Infantry
nodes.x: A Union officer seconded to the UNEL, of the Polish line that never learned when to stop: wounded, decorated, wounded again and cheerful about all of it. He commands the Directorate of Unified Security's ground forces in 2312.

nodes.t: Drafted the Orbital Draft
nodes.x: A Geneva treaty lawyer on the Secretary-General's staff, who drafted the Geneva Orbital Draft, including its third clause, later the Lunar Mandate's first rule. By her own account she saw her text pinned up in the lunar yard's mess before she saw it adopted.

nodes.t: Governance
nodes.x: Treats the UNEL's charter as a machine to be optimised rather than a moral text, cutting bureaucracy with surgical precision or turning it into a shield as required, and regards negotiation as inefficient noise. In 2312 he chairs the waste regulation committee and formally asks whether anyone salvaging the war wrecks holds a permit.

nodes.t: The Tangier collective
nodes.x: A Moroccan mechanic in the Tangier collective's assembly, which elects the Tramuntana's crew and eats at one table. She is known for settling arguments over dinner before they reach the vote.

nodes.t: Department of People Resources · Governance
nodes.x: Works through people rather than paper, turning rapport, memory and quiet pressure into agreements that no statute could enforce. In her view bureaucracy is camouflage for the real bargains underneath. In 2312 she represents the UNEL on the Minangkabau inquiry.

nodes.t: The Gran Chaco ceasefire
nodes.x: A Brazilian Army officer posted to the Gran Chaco ceasefire line, who watched Ruairí Ó Dálaigh's white squad keep two armies apart for a year and drew from it the conclusion that order holds where the strong guarantee it.

nodes.t: Solar Court
nodes.x: A judge of conflict, terrorism and space law from what was Brazil. Her rulings favour established powers over fragile frontier settlements; in public this is legal conservatism, and in private it rests on a belief that order must be protected from premature independence. She signs the Solar Court's opinion against the Union's Bolivia motion.

nodes.t: An Antarctic open city
nodes.x: Keeps an Antarctic station open through the war as one of the UN's open cities, trading fuel and prisoners with whichever front comes past.

nodes.t: Solar Court
nodes.x: A Tasmanian specialist in environmental and extraction law, with a carefully kept reputation for moderation. On the record his rulings are quietly inconsistent and shaped by circumstance, and he holds that ambiguity is what keeps a court legitimate.

nodes.t: Left Grey Lantern
nodes.x: Ingrid Solheim's niece, who learned contracts at Grey Lantern's desk and leaves for the UN in the war, saying she wants to work for the only client every side lets into the ruins.

nodes.t: UN Secretariat · Governance
nodes.x: Joined the UN as an intern and has lived by its charter ever since. She is known for a clean record and for paperwork that is cleaner still, and the Secretariat relies on her as its respected neutral mediator.

nodes.t: Drove the white convoys
nodes.x: A Swedish volunteer who drove a white-painted Copperbelt walker with the first white convoys, and was the last out of every town the raids reached.

nodes.t: Migration and refugees · Governance
nodes.x: Holds that fieldwork is where the real work gets done. He is on first-name terms with world leaders and warlords alike, and is noted as the last to leave whenever an embassy or outpost is evacuated, much like the convoy driver he is named for. He runs the UNEL's refugee and migration desk.

nodes.t: India's wartime bioresearch
nodes.x: A scientist in India's wartime bioresearch programme. He grew up through twenty years of raids by the first enhanced soldiers, and what he wanted was a weapon against the enhanced, and an Earth that would never need one.

nodes.t: Director of the Lunar Spire
nodes.x: A biologist of human enhancement who directs the Lunar Vacuum Research Spire and keeps its last AMX/9 samples. In 2312 a joint audit finds he has been receiving field-test data through a relay at Mercury. He is arrested, and gives no motive. ███ █████ ████ ███████ ████ █████████ ███ ██ █████.

nodes.t: Solar Court · Humanity First
nodes.x: Opens the Solar Court, orders the audit of the Lunar Spire and asks the General Hall to renounce weapons of mass destruction, then leads the UNEL's Humanity First wing through the attacks that follow.

nodes.t: Washington's man at the Forgeworks
nodes.x: Arthur's son, who was on Phobos with the Rapid Defence Force the day it took the Forgeworks with one shot fired. Washington has run the yard since, and by 2327 Callum runs it for the Navy: American hulls bound for Mars and Jupiter lose their seals there, under the eyes of a staff that was Colony One's fifteen years ago. His reports are frank about that staff, and he reckons he can trust about half of them.

nodes.t: The ship that can't be hacked
nodes.x: Professor Silla's child, who grew up on the same story of the evacuation runway and drew a different lesson from it: a ship is only as safe as its crew. Taqqiq commands an Independence-class battleship, air-gapped from end to end on the Professor's own designs, and refits it at the Far Roads before every run past the Moon. Its crew call it the quietest ship in the Navy, since nothing aboard is allowed to talk to anything outside it.

nodes.t: Reading the clause aloud
nodes.x: Luz Garza's granddaughter, Ada's cousin, and the first water judge to sit on New Philadelphia's high court. The charter her family carried to Mars says there is no Martian war without Washington, and by 2327 every Constitutionalist wants to know what it means if Washington says no and the war comes anyway. Paloma will be the one to answer, and has let it be known that she reads the clause the way its authors wrote it.

nodes.t: The son who stayed
nodes.x: Silas Vane's son, who was offered a berth with the fleet when it left Mars and turned it down. He stays in the north through the partisan years, hiding weapons, burning records and leading Dustline cells in the tunnels under the Bastion, where the charges are named after Bram Okafor. Washington has had a file open on him for years without getting much further than his name.

nodes.t: Holding Deimos
nodes.x: Eric Hart's daughter, taught to fly by Theo Lindqvist, and the officer who commands the Directorate's guns on Deimos after the Union fails to take them in 2312. She keeps the Union's old berths open on the Directorate's terms and lets its hulls refit there when she chooses, and she fights the way the Harts always have.

nodes.t: Finishing what she started
nodes.x: Ana Lubov's nephew, who joined the Innovation Bureau to work for her and found himself following her instead, picking up each revolution she abandoned and making it safe to use. By 2327 half the Directorate's fleet runs on things Ana invented and Yarik finished. Ana has always thought him slow, though the fleet's engineers are generally glad that he is.

nodes.t: Keeper of the Trojans
nodes.x: Sunday's daughter, who has run security at the Trojan anchorages since the Union took them in 2312. The rocks are captured, their docks are Hanse ships and their garrisons are drawn from every corner of the Union, and she runs them as her father taught her, acting first and leaving the reports to explain it afterwards.

nodes.t: The Union that needs no colony
nodes.x: Michel-Patrique's niece, from the office her family founded, and the author of the Union's policy beyond the Moon after 2312: no colony of its own, anchorages instead, and the Directorate as a neighbour rather than a province. The old guard call it a retreat, and she has spent years in committee arguing that it is the next phase of the Union rather than the end of one. By 2327 she sits on the council that will decide what the Union does when the crisis comes.

nodes.t: Hunting torches
nodes.x: Lin Xuefeng's daughter, who grew up aboard the Dragon Aerie while her father advised the machine that replaced him. She commands a Jianwei-class frigate, built after 2312 to hunt ships flying on unlicensed torches, and refits it at the Juno berth China never gave up. At her request the ship carries a human tactical officer, which is unusual on a frigate of its class.

nodes.t: The carrier's mind
nodes.x: The next of the line, given command of the Tianmen-class carrier and its fusion frames when the ship is commissioned. Like 236/H it has flashes of caprice built in, so that no enemy can predict it; unlike 236/H it was trained on the Martian crisis, and it has opinions about what its predecessor got wrong. Major Zhou Lan, who flies the Zhulong, reports to it.

nodes.t: Trading with the faithful
nodes.x: Kalani's son, who was aboard when his father's caravan met the black ship from Pluto in 2312. Makoa was quicker than the other houses to see a market rather than a shipload of refugees, and he spends the next decade carrying the Communion's archives, ice and pilgrims across the Belt for a share of everything that follows. The sun graffiti that later covers Ceres first appeared on the walls of his family's warehouses.

nodes.t: Pricing the crisis
nodes.x: Dr Xiao Tseng Lai's niece, augmented and wired into a lattice of her own, who runs the house's forward markets after her aunt moves up. The Syndicate builds no new battle line after 2312, only the claim carriers its houses use to collect debts, and it sells to everyone who does build one. By 2327 Xiao An's desk is pricing contracts on the Greater Solar Crisis before anyone has fired, and her prices are the best forecast in the system.

nodes.t: Fitting the Second Seal
nodes.x: Bartholomew Morgan's daughter, who commands an Assessor-class cutter on Earth's approaches after the Signing. She boards warships that would rather she didn't and fits the Second Seal to their plants, and past the Moon, where she has no right to board anyone, she asks anyway and logs whatever answer she gets.

nodes.t: Keeping the file
nodes.x: Magnus Furyk's son, of the Polish line that never learned when to stop, who served on the Directorate of Unified Security team that found the Jupiter Directive. By 2327 he keeps its file, and asks the General Hall every year what it intends to do with it. Every year he is told the matter is under review.

nodes.t: The guard at Mercury
nodes.x: A descendant of Arkady Belov of the siege trains, who commands the Burya-K frames guarding the Mercury dock. In 2312 she watches the Eurasian battlegroup destroy the abandoned Indian station in high orbit, and is asked by the UNEL's observers what was aboard it. She tells them it was never part of the dock.

nodes.t: Oath-sworn
nodes.x: Vera's son, who swore the Nashik Oath in Russian and flies a Vityaz, the Staya's heir. His augmentation is equipment owed to his unit, and the unit owes him a pension it has never been late with. He has cousins in the Ashva Compact, and his orders are not to contact them.

nodes.t: Minister for the colonies at Jupiter
nodes.x: A Delhi minister who governs the Ascendancy's enhanced colonies at Jupiter from months away, and visits the joint anchorage on Europa more often than any minister before him. His name is in the file the UNEL found. He says he has never read the Jupiter Directive, and the Hegemony, if it exists, has never confirmed whether he is one of them.

nodes.t: Holding the Eros dock
nodes.x: A descendant of Amina Diallo, the Commonwealth's founder who wrote influence without occupation In 2312 she is a junior officer aboard the Chergui frigate the Commonwealth sends to watch the Union's blockade of Eros, and afterwards she commands the Eros dock, the Commonwealth's only one this side of Jupiter, and runs its relief convoys out to Europa. People on Eros like to point out that her frigate's hospital bay has treated more Union sailors than Commonwealth ones.

nodes.t: Selling the Gharbi
nodes.x: Head of the Khartoum export office, which has sold frames to half of Earth since the war. In the 2320s she follows the Khamaseen with the Gharbi into South America and the Middle East, and keeps no bases there; the Commonwealth, they say in Khartoum, has no need of them. Every power that hears the rumours of a sixth Earth power looks first at her order books.

nodes.t: Guardianship
nodes.x: Keeper Nala Osei's daughter, who sits on the life-systems councils and speaks for their oldest word, guardianship. She votes for every measure that gives the councils more say in how Umoja's people are cultivated and cared for. Her mother still flies the Kinsman, and is the only person on Ganymede who argues with her in public.

nodes.t: Bound to the Kindred
nodes.x: Zawadi's son, bonded from childhood to a Kindred, the frame lined with mats that eat Jupiter's radiation. By 2327 he leads the frames aboard a Mbegu seeding carrier, which lands on Callisto and grows a fortress where it stands. The Ashva watch every landing, and Baraka, who sees no reason to be unfriendly about it, waves at them.

nodes.t: One licence for everyone
nodes.x: Born on Ascension's stations to a Kenyan crew family, he was given the bone and muscle therapies its low-gravity children got as a matter of course. He came down to Earth at twelve and found that no bloc would license him to work, serve or, in some places, marry. In 2183 he led the Geneva Walk, asking for one licence every bloc would honour, and called the movement Umoja: unity. In 2186 the United States passed Unaltered Crews, and the movement began to break. When the Commonwealth put the grafted aboard the Hafun ships, he went with them: if they go, I go. On Ganymede he lived to see strength win, and let it.

nodes.t: The keepers' rule, kept
nodes.x: Amos's daughter, born two years before the Walk and raised on the Hospital Safinas among the grafted. On Ganymede she took the keepers' rule as her own: what is grown is cared for, never commanded. She lost the Ganymede Split to her brother, kept her seat on the life-systems councils, and spent forty years turning them into the one thread every tribe still answers to. The Oseis are her line.

nodes.t: Strength through strength
nodes.x: Amos's son, grafted at seventeen on the North African Front, who rode with the raid cadres because they were the ones who won. On Ganymede he led the Lodges in the Ganymede Split, and his father, who could have stopped him with a word, said nothing. He taught that a body you grew is a body you command, and that Earth, which wouldn't license them, has no say in what they become.

nodes.t: Speaks for the Lodges
nodes.x: Jabari's descendant on one side and Khalid Osman's on the other, and in 2327 the captain the Lodges send to every council. She flies a Kith grown to her own measure and carries a grown sting the keepers won't name. She trades with Garuda Works in the morning and hunts its sworn pairs at night, and sees no contradiction in either.

nodes.t: Down through the ice
nodes.x: Commander Devika Rao's daughter, raised on Europa among the sworn pairs, and captain of the first Antardhara carrier to melt its way down through twenty kilometres of ice into the ocean beneath, with her brother flying her lead frame. The Ascendancy watched her go down from the joint anchorage, and began building ships to follow her.

nodes.t: The Garuda's designer
nodes.x: Chief designer at Garuda Works, and descended from the Mitsurugi exiles who left Japan through Vladivostok. Her Garuda runs on a frame fusion core the Compact built for itself, and it is closer to flying than Beijing believes. Rahim Qureshi's lance flies her prototypes, and she follows every rumour out of the Zhulong's trials.

nodes.t: The Primorye crews
nodes.x: A welder from Vladivostok's yards, one of the Far Eastern crews the orbital yards sent home with cold and radiation therapies that no ministry in Moscow would license. He walked to Geneva in 2183 with the Far Eastern contingent and came home sure that asking had been the mistake: the strong should defend the weak, not wait for permission to. When the Hakobune landed at Vladivostok, his Primorye crews hid the Nashik pilots from Moscow's officers and the Mitsurugi engineers from Beijing's agents, and went up with them. The veche was his idea, and its habit of arguing about everything is his legacy.

nodes.t: The ride the Ascendancy disowned
nodes.x: Lev's great-granddaughter, who led her akhara into an Ascendancy settlement's cells on Europa to free three strays held for trial, and was back before dawn. The Ascendancy pulled down her akhara's hall. A year later one of the three killed a family on Io, and she rode out alone to bring him in. She never said whether she thought she had been wrong, and the akharas still argue about it.

nodes.t: Rode out at Himalia
nodes.x: Darya's descendant, raised in the akhara she founded after her hall came down, and the lance leader who took the crew off the hauler at Himalia and crippled the Jianwei that had left them there. He was still on the base when the Ascendancy's warning came, and was the last to leave it. He has never been sure whether the Ascendancy betrayed the Compact that day, or saved it from him.

nodes.t: Tending the Long Mirrors
nodes.x: Sister Aurore Vey's grandson, who flies a Mirrorwright at Uranus, turning the kilometre mirrors to catch a sun that is barely a bright star. The work is devotion, and he does not see the difference between keeping the mirrors and praying. His grandmother is still on watch somewhere further out in the dark, and in all the long years of her watch she has been woken only four times.

nodes.t: The faith comes calling
nodes.x: Descended from the Andean refugees who fled south to the ice during the war, she became the Communion's envoy to the inner system after the Pluto ship came home. She travels with Makoa Stevens's caravans, and she preaches on Ceres, where the sun graffiti began. When a Testament-class battleship appears, it has usually come because she arranged it.

mysteries.label: Mysteries
mysteries.intro: Plot hooks for game masters, generation by generation: places nobody in the atlas has reached, fleet actions nobody has claimed, rogue machines nobody has noticed. None is answered anywhere in the atlas, and lines join hooks that may be connected.
turns: An emptied seed vault, stolen identities and salvagers in the graveyard orbit: the pre-mech world already had trades that no bloc measured.
Unflagged raiders on the lunar lanes, a rescue flotilla with forged transponders, a valley off both maps. Not everyone in the war fought for a bloc.
A century of peace on paper leaves Saturn closed, a Chinese ship past Jupiter and two hundred and thirty-six rogue AIs on a register nobody publishes.
By 2327 the places the five powers never reached are starting to make demands of their own.
