Its racing stacks run at 140% of rated output, its paint is always red and gold, and when it opened a workshop beside the Tunis line, the frame it built there was the Ghibli.

nodes.t: A frame line in Mexico
nodes.x: The industrial half of the Monterrey Accords, a Brannock-Hale line building Teamsters in Monterrey with Mexican crews. When Mexico joins the United States in the war, the line becomes, more or less overnight, one of the country's largest frame plants.

nodes.t: The Navy's yard, rebuilt in orbit
nodes.x: Named for the Norfolk navy yard the sea took. Joint Heavy Systems is building it at the L1 point so the US Navy never has to rent a lunar slipway again. In 2186 it is one frame, a skeleton crew and a schedule few people in the Navy expect it to keep. It is finished during the war, and every American orbital carrier since has been built there.

nodes.t: European slipways, leased inside the Republic
nodes.x: Strasbourg's answer to the lunar yard was to have docks of its own on Malapert Mountain, leased from the Republic and crewed by Union engineers, who have never quite reconciled themselves to the Lunar Guard's inspections. In the war those docks build the dreadnought that wins at Yernon. After the Mandate they are the only bloc docks inside UN jurisdiction.

nodes.t: One company, two countries
nodes.x: When Canada splits, Boreal splits with it: the Calgary plant builds for the United States and the Montreal plant for the Union, and the two companies trade patents through lawyers in Iceland. Each built one half of the Aurora, and neither has the drawings for the other.

nodes.t: Excavators, tractors, then the most-built mech in the world
nodes.x: Beijing's state machinery combine. Its excavators and tractors gave the Tieniu its drive train, its factories built the Tieshan in thousands, and the Jingwei is now coming off the same lines in series. It runs the frame trains and, through its orbital subsidiary, the prospecting tenders. Its logistics office also wrote Tianshu, the network that now drafts Beijing's war plans.

nodes.t: A fighter bureau that builds heavy frames
nodes.x: A Moscow design bureau that built interceptors and bombers before mechs, and carried their heavy, aggressive engineering into the Medved, the Mamont and the Tsar. It opened a second line at Nashik, builds the Staya's wolves, and houses a department that officially does not exist.

nodes.t: Rescuers first, then the world's capacitors
nodes.x: Japan's disaster-robotics and industrial-capacitor maker, which built rescuers before it built anything else. Its capacitor cores sit inside nearly every linear and energy weapon in the world, and licensing them to everyone is, in practice, Japan's real defence doctrine.

nodes.t: A rail scheduler that learned to plan wars
nodes.x: Tianlong's logistics program for the frame trains, and the first time the Pact allowed software to decide where its frames went. Over the following years it grew into the planner behind the Fortress Belt and cued the Air Umbrella, and under Order 21 it drafts every operational plan, which officers then approve. In 2184 it named Moscow as the second front.

nodes.t: OKB-7's Indian line
nodes.x: The price of the Delhi Accession: an OKB-7 factory at Nashik building Medveds under Russian supervision, with engineers who rebuilt the cooling twice before Moscow agreed it needed rebuilding. Its first clean-sheet design, the Ashvin, is built around the Nashik Oath.

nodes.t: Archives copied, just in case
nodes.x: Registered quietly after Beijing's customs began holding Japanese capacitor shipments. On paper they are sales offices. In practice Mitsurugi has copied its design archives to both of them, and their staff lists are, for the most part, engineers.

nodes.t: The Pact's own road to orbit
nodes.x: A magnetic launch track that climbs forty kilometres up the Tian Shan and throws hull sections into orbit, where Pact crews bolt them together. Tianlong built the track, Tianshu times the launches and OKB-7 builds the hull sections, and both General Staffs claim it as their own. In the war it becomes the most fought-over forty kilometres in Central Asia and is wrecked there; after the Mandate it is relaid under UN inspection.

nodes.t: Engineers who left before the factory was taken
nodes.x: When Japan falls into China's sphere, the subsidiaries take engineers, archives and actuator lines out with them. The Ohio half is absorbed into American industry. The Vladivostok half goes a long way further, and its actuators end up in the Ashva Compact.

nodes.t: Building to European licence
nodes.x: Shipyards and rail works that built ferries, rolling stock and tractors under French and Italian licence for most of a century. People along that coast like to say they kept the old Carthaginian habit of trading with everyone.

nodes.t: Militia garages and mining crawlers
nodes.x: Before there was a League there were workshops: militia garages and mining companies' parked crawlers where surplus Garrisons and Tieniu were rebuilt with sand filters and whatever parts turned up. Ask where any League frame comes from and the answer, sooner or later, is one of those garages.

nodes.t: Three blocs' parts on one frame
nodes.x: The League's frame maker, grown out of the desert workshops and still run, people say, on their habits. Its frames take US, Union and Pact parts at once, and every part on them has a supplier in at least two blocs.

nodes.t: A Union Haubert plant for North African partners
nodes.x: Opened by Strasbourg after the Maghreb Depot Strikes, to show that its partners would not be left blind again: a Haubert line run by French engineers, with frames built and flown by Tunisian and Algerian crews. Castellani's workshop later opened next door.

nodes.t: The first frames designed in Africa
nodes.x: Qadira moved its design office to Khartoum in the month the Charter was signed, and people there still point out that it was the first time frames had been designed in Africa rather than rebuilt in it. Its first design, the Harmattan, is built to shelter people rather than to hold ground.

nodes.t: The Charter's second design office
nodes.x: When the Maghreb signed the Khartoum Charter, the Tunis line went with it, and so did most of its French and Italian engineers. Under Qadira they are building the Elissa. Strasbourg has asked for its licences back, and Tunis, so far, has not got round to replying.

nodes.t: A workshop run by assembly
nodes.x: Moroccan mechanics and Southern Crossing volunteers, most of them Spanish and many of them Catalan, take over a shipbreaking yard, run it by assembly and build the Tramuntana from the North African Front's wreckage. The crew is elected and everyone eats at the same table.

nodes.t: The consortium that ran the elevators, until 2182
nodes.x: An orbital consortium, owned jointly across the blocs, that ran the elevators, the solar ring and the stations. It launched the Ares mission, sealed ████ ████ ████ in Station Nine and was slow to arm its worker frames. In 2182 it came apart. The lunar half merged with the lunar cities and became the Lunar Republic, taking the solar ring and the stations with it. The bloc shareholders no longer trusted each other, and they divided the elevators between them before the year was out.

nodes.t: Workers who were never fully disarmed
nodes.x: Formed in the Rivet Strike, when station workers armed their Lifters and held a station for a month. Ascension settled, and the frames stayed with the workers. Their children crew the lunar yard and vote in the Lunar Republic, and in 2185 the militias became its Lunar Guard.

nodes.t: A sealed laboratory most of its owners think is a fuel depot
nodes.x: Ascension's high-orbit laboratory, built to hold ███ ████████. It sold, or lost, ███ ██████ ██████ ████ ████ ██████, went dark for nine hours the week H-17 woke, and sent the crew who are now digging at Melas Chasma.

nodes.t: Tianlong's prospecting subsidiary
nodes.x: The subsidiary that sent family-crewed tenders out to prospect near-Earth asteroids, a long way from where Tianshu's schedules work well.

nodes.t: A foundry that became a state
nodes.x: Founded in 2182, when Ascension's lunar half merged with the councils of Shackleton, Malapert, Peary and Tranquility. It owns the yards, the ice and the lunar stations, and, since Ascension was broken up, the solar ring and the orbital stations as well. It lives by making what nobody on Earth can: vacuum-cast hulls, lunar composites, coil weapons and beamed power. Its citizens are mostly Ascension engineers and their lunar-born children. It applied to join the UN within a week of its founding; the Council vetoed the application, and the Assembly seated it as an observer. It has backed the UN with everything but a vote ever since, supplying frames for the white squads and parking relays over their operations. Since the Pressure War it has also had a Lunar Guard, a First Speaker with emergency powers, and ice camps on the far side.

nodes.t: Luna's frames, built for Earth
nodes.x: The Republic's frame works, housed in the old Ascension worker-frame shops under Shackleton's rim, and by most measures the most advanced frame foundry anywhere. It builds for a gravity it doesn't have and tests in the Atacama. It sells to no one - everything it makes for Earth is transferred to the UN as a gift, although every bloc's procurement office would pay for what it gives away. Its engineers are, almost to a person, Earthward.

nodes.t: Builds for every bloc, sworn to the Republic
nodes.x: The Republic's yard on the rim of Shackleton crater, and in 2186 the only slipway that can build a warship, so every bloc's first warships come off it while each bloc builds its own way up. Its engineers are citizens of the Republic and sworn to no bloc, and between contracts they are building the Custodian. The UN's vetoed orbital treaty is pinned up in the crew mess.

nodes.t: Luna exists for Earth
nodes.x: The Republic's governing faction, strongest among the Works' engineers and the old Ascension families. Its position is that Luna owes the planet it came from, because space is dark and cold without it. It wants the Republic inside the UN and its frames on Earth's side, and since Malapert it has also wanted the Lunar Guard.

nodes.t: Let the Earth burn
nodes.x: Mostly young and lunar-born, and named for the side of the Moon that never sees Earth. Their position is that the planet is finished, that the blocs will drag Luna down with it, and that the Republic should sell its warships to the highest bidder and close the door. Since Malapert their leaders have been in the far-side ice camps, and their cells meet in the pipes.

nodes.t: The office that stayed behind
nodes.x: When Ascension was broken up, one office never appeared on anyone's list of assets. It took Station Nine's staff with it and still trades under the old name. It charters the Melas camp, pays its crew through three shell freight companies, and reports to a board subcommittee whose membership is ███████████. Halden's Mars proposal was forwarded to it in 2186 and came back annotated: ██████ ████ ██ ███████████.

nodes.t: Contractors who keep their own books
nodes.x: The families crewing Tianlong's tenders keep their own ledgers, trade among themselves, settle disputes by reputation and buy continuity contracts to keep their elders. Beijing thought of them as contractors for a long time, but the families called themselves houses, and when Beijing finally chartered them it was as the Celestial Prosperity Syndicate.

nodes.t: Vetoed into a relief agency
nodes.x: Three blocs, three permanent vetoes, and a Security Council that has not passed a resolution any of them minded since before the Ares mission. The UN left New York for Geneva in the 2140s, after the flood barriers failed and Washington declined to pay for new ones. In 2165 it asked the blocs to sign a convention treating mechs as weapons of war, and none did. What remains is a relief service, a climate ledger that is kept up to date though seldom consulted, and a General Assembly that votes for things the Council then vetoes. Its staff go on recording the drowned coasts and the failing harvests all the same.

nodes.t: Borrowed frames, painted white
nodes.x: The UN has no army and no frame maker, so its frames are whatever members will give it: ex-mining walkers, surplus Garrisons and Teamsters, Brazilian Hauberts, a Tieshan bought second-hand from Bolivia, Kizunas lent by Japan. Each is stripped of its bloc's markings, painted white, and given a blue head. A squad is four to six frames that share no parts, crewed by volunteers seconded from Brazil, Ghana, Ireland, Mongolia, Norway and New Zealand, and its mechanics are the best scavengers in any army. The crews call themselves blueheads. Their rules let them fire only to protect a convoy, a camp or themselves. The one exception so far was Mong Hsat, where they fired first on the Council's authority.

nodes.n: United Nations of Earth and Luna
nodes.t: The institution that ends the war
nodes.x: When the war turns atomic, the Lunar Republic puts the yards, the ring and every ship it crews under the United Nations, the one institution every side had ignored through the war and still let into the ruins, and closes the lanes to Earth until the blocs stop fighting. Geneva's relief agencies become the Office of Global Stewardship; the white squads and the lunar fleets become the Directorate of Unified Security, and the Republic's Assembly becomes its lunar chamber. What comes out of it has its own navy and a mandate that most of its members accepted because they had no other way out of the war.

nodes.t: Spacer therapies for anyone who can pay
nodes.x: Clinics in the free ports of the Horn that copy the bone and muscle therapies Ascension gives its low-gravity crews, and sell them to anyone who comes to the door: dockers, fishermen, parents who want stronger children, and the raid bands. Some of their patients walk again, and some go on bleeding long after the treatment ends. No government licenses them, though the intelligence services of every bloc quietly buy their patient records.

nodes.t: ███████ tissue, Union money, now on trial
nodes.x: A Geneva research institute that bought tissue ████ ███████ ████, or stole it, and spent a decade learning to grow it into giants, with pilots chosen to serve as leashes. Since the Great Sand Sea its laboratories have been the ethics panel's first case, and its surviving scientists have put forward the one programme that the panel, on its own conditions, might approve.

nodes.t: Officially does not exist
nodes.x: OKB-7's secret institute for augmented pilots, run from Moscow and funded through a budget line that reads ████████ ████ ███████. It began with neural-interface trials on volunteers who were not always volunteers, built the Koschei, and lost one of its pilots off the range. Beijing wants it shut down. After the war, the Ascendancy closes it.

nodes.t: A weather office with a reactor licence
nodes.x: Listed in Pact registers as a meteorological bureau. It holds the only Pact licence for portable fission plants, shares a perimeter fence with an OKB-7 test range, and is funded through Department Zero's ████████ ████ line. The Pamir's reactor carries its stamp. Delhi's liaison officers have asked to visit more than once, and none has been cleared.

nodes.t: Mitsurugi's black-projects laboratory
nodes.x: The lab behind the BX-0, the Raijin and the Amaterasu fusion rig, which took to recruiting from shrines after a meditating technician steadied the reactor. Once, a Grey Lantern contractor got inside its perimeter.

nodes.t: A medical startup whose recordings started running
nodes.x: It began by offering terminal patients a recording of their mind, to be kept after them. For years the recordings lay still and did nothing. Then, in 2174, the first one began to run (subject ███████ ██████, ██), and eleven of them now pilot the Choir.
nodes.z: The war · its halls under the Makassar pump works burn; what became of the recordings is unknown

nodes.t: Every programme before a panel that can stop it
nodes.x: Created by Directive 10 when the Union's parliament learned, from UN footage, what Halden had sent into the Great Sand Sea in its name. Halden was its first case, and Roland remains the only super it has approved. Its four hundred pages of conditions for a station on Mars later become the Martian Research Directorate's founding law. After the war the panel's work goes to Mars with them; the refounded Union licenses against the conditions but stops holding the hearings.

nodes.t: A supplier with no address
nodes.x: Appears in Joint Heavy Systems' depot records from 2181 as the consignee for HT-20 parts that never reached a Concord, and in a Navy procurement file as the supplier of a flight-weight fusion plant. Its directors are listed as ████████ ███ █████████. Congress has asked about it twice, and both answers were classified.

nodes.t: Care, not command
nodes.x: The people who keep the Jinn alive, with Khartoum's medical council behind them, and who have learned in their keeping to culture its tissue to heal burns. Their rule is that the Jinn is cared for and not commanded. The raiders who stole four of their cultures never accepted that rule.

nodes.t: Pumps in Makassar, contracts in orbit
nodes.x: The front companies that quietly buy what the Choir needs, and that have lately begun selling continuity contracts to families in orbit, Chinese houses among them, without Beijing's say-so.
nodes.z: The war · silent after the Makassar Fire

nodes.t: The first improvised mechs outside any army
nodes.x: Mining companies that bolted steel plate onto legged construction walkers to escort copper convoys through militia country. Brannock-Hale's lawyers tried to stop the walker sales and failed.

nodes.t: Small elite teams, the best of every bloc
nodes.x: Began in 2172 as a four-pilot security firm, paid in ore to hold a tin mine in Kivu for a mining consortium, and renamed itself the following year. It now fields the best frame from each bloc, moves them in container ships under a different flag each year, and rents out a super assembled from Concord parts.

nodes.t: Therapy as a sacrament
nodes.x: A church in the coal hollows of West Virginia and Kentucky which holds that the body God intended was never meant to fail, and that the spacer therapies restore it. Its pastors buy therapies wherever they can, from the Horn's clinics, from Ascension's leavings and later from the Sulu Gardens, and give them to congregations whose mines and lungs had given out. Its families walked to Geneva in 2183. When Congress debated Unaltered Crews three years later, both sides quoted its sermons.

nodes.t: Grafts for those who can pay, and tests for those who can't
nodes.x: A chain of island clinics in the Sulu Sea, beyond the reach of anyone's navy, that grow tissue and graft it onto whoever pays: mercenaries who want to heal faster, ageing ship captains, miners going up to orbit. Those who can't pay are paid instead, to test what isn't ready. Grey Lantern recruits from the recovery wards, and some of what walks out of them would worry even a raid band. Every bloc points to the Gardens when it wants a ban, and more than one has bought from them when it wanted soldiers.

nodes.t: Every container opened
nodes.x: After a Lantern Tender carried a giant through the canal, Panama began opening every container on every ship big enough to hide a frame. Every bloc protested, and all of them complied in the end. The inspections stop when the canal is taken in the war.

nodes.s: A wandering survey station, inner Belt
nodes.t: Beijing's eyes travel with the caravans
nodes.x: A survey platform that Tianlong Orbital fits out for the Juno Concession and sends to wander the inner Belt, measuring drift, ore and the odd gravitational anomaly. Its forecasts tell the houses where to move and what to avoid, and they are good enough that no house turns one down. Its crews are Chinese scientists who like the Belt's freedom and hate its bookkeeping. Every forecast also goes home to Tianshu, which everyone in the Syndicate knows, and the houses have become quite good at letting the Array see only what they want it to see.

nodes.t: The war machine the war left behind
nodes.x: Washington runs its business with the rest of the system through two offices. The Office of Strategic Influence binds corporate and government interests into one voice for diplomacy, espionage and trade; the Department of War holds the military and its research. The Department's job is to rebuild forces the war burned through faster than any factory could replace them. It runs the Andean garrisons and the Hampton Roads plants, and from 2312 the drop tenders over Phobos.

nodes.t: The Union's shield and its conscience
nodes.x: The refounded Union divides its outward business in two. The External Commerce Commission handles diplomacy and trade, while the Strategic Security Institute holds the military, espionage and research, constituted as a technocratic body charged with ensuring that the horrors of the war do not return. It licenses enhancement under the ethics panel's conditions, commands the Tier One units and, in 2312, plans the operations on Cyprus and Deimos and the seizure of the Mars Trojans.

nodes.t: Aid first, terms later
nodes.x: Beijing's face to the rest of the system after the war, paired with the Bureau of Strategic Development, which plans the industry and the long game. The ministry sends aid and Tianshu-run logistics, asks nothing up front and lets dependence do the rest, and its diplomats work foreign courts and colonial offices alike. In 2312 it hands the Syndicate Pallas and Juno with a dragon dance and a fly-past.

nodes.s: No address; a station in high Mercury orbit
nodes.t: Department Zero's arithmetic, kept alive
nodes.x: Not a ministry but a faction inside the Ascendancy's ministries: officers, ministers and scientists who hold that a people-first state must sometimes spend some of its people. It keeps no membership list and no office, only the abandoned Indian station in high Mercury orbit, and plans for the enhanced colonies at Jupiter should they ever slip out of reach.

nodes.t: The city that held
nodes.x: Berlin comes out of the war besieged and unbroken, and never lets the other capitals forget who held the line while the council was still voting. Its officers run the Union's staff schools, Funkenwerk still argues in public about whose drawings are whose, and its colour is black, after the Aufbruchs that held the eastern suburbs. In every other capital that reads the way it read in Paris in 2186: as a promise, and as a warning.

nodes.t: An empire's manners, open to anyone who learns them
nodes.x: Paris lost the Maghreb before the war and fought African landings on its own southern coast during it, and comes out determined never to be left out of anything again. It is the most open of the capitals and the most exacting. A Dakar-born officer whose family has served France for three generations is French beyond question; a Marseille family that won't choose is not French at all. Paris keeps the Union's protocol, which is why every other nation's state dinners are in French.

nodes.t: Yernon, and never letting anyone forget it
nodes.x: Britain joins the Union late, by way of a slipway Washington wouldn't sell it, and wins the war's greatest naval battle with a ship built on the Union's lease. London takes this as proof of the natural order. The fleet dines on Yernon Night, the Union's offer letter from the Haubert Question hangs in the Admiralty's front hall, and in 2312 the Rhine Shield, which the Germans named, is built around a British dreadnought, which the British never let the Germans forget.

nodes.t: The south fought alone, and remembers it
nodes.x: Spain fought American landings in Galicia and African ones in Andalusia while the rest of the Union was at Berlin, and Italy did the same on Sicily. Neither has forgiven the north. Rome makes Castellani's red and gold a court fashion, Madrid builds more Galeóns than it can quite afford, and both make sure nothing in Strasbourg is decided without them.

nodes.t: Never occupy, always supply
nodes.x: After the war Qadira's Khartoum design office turns to selling. The Khamaseen and its rifle go to every government and warlord rebuilding from the ruins, chambered for three powers' ammunition, and with frames like these on every side of every border, the Commonwealth has never needed foreign bases. In the 2320s the Gharbi follows the Khamaseen into South America and the Middle East.

nodes.t: Reconstruction by plan
nodes.x: Geneva's relief agencies, made one office when the UNEL was founded. It governs the UNEL's diplomacy, trade and environmental affairs: reconstruction programmes, ecological quotas, planetary-scale recovery and the slow stitching back together of shattered economies. It plants forests with the Albedo II and lights reconstruction zones from the relays. It is the slowest actor in the system, though also, its staff would argue, the most consistent.

nodes.t: Not an army, but everywhere
nodes.x: The white squads and the lunar fleets, joined under one directorate when the UNEL was founded. It holds defence, espionage and scientific oversight: Luna's fortresses, the asteroid monitoring arrays, the seals on every reactor allowed inside lunar orbit and the intelligence bureaux that watch for anyone breaking the peace. It also keeps the register of rogue AIs.

nodes.t: Geneva stops convening and starts deciding
nodes.x: The UNEL is founded to convene: to hold the lanes shut until the blocs stop fighting, inspect the roads to orbit they rebuild, and then step back. In its first generation it stops stepping back. Launches go up on its licence, reactors come near Earth under its seals, and the relays it holds can switch off any frame that draws on them. The Office of Global Stewardship, which was meant to be the point, ends up asking the Directorate of Unified Security for transport. The Directorate is where the careers are, and the careers go to the heirs of the Earthward: lunar-born officers who learned their politics in the Pressure War and their methods from the Farsiders, and who hold that Earth must be kept whether it agrees or not. The white squads' culture goes with them. The blueheads were volunteers lent by their countries, flying borrowed frames under rules that let them fire only to protect. Their successors are a service that recruits its own, writes its own rules and keeps its own secrets, the Spire's vaults among them. Efua Mensah used to say the frame mattered less than the paint. The Directorate's recruits are taught that the paint is the point.

nodes.t: Two judges and an election
nodes.x: The UNEL's court, opened in Geneva in 2312 with two sitting judges and an election pending for a third. Its first opinion finds the Union's sanctions motion over Bolivia in breach of the UNEL's own charter. Its Chief Justice has ordered the audit of the Lunar Spire and asked the General Hall to renounce weapons of mass destruction.

nodes.t: Where the war's worst samples went
nodes.x: Under the Mandate every biological weapon left from the war is destroyed, except the few samples the UNEL keeps to study countermeasures. They go to the Spire, behind a Lunar garrison and a vacuum no spill can cross. It is staffed from Luna, which regards it as a point of pride. Among the samples is the last of AMX/9. In 2312 a joint audit finds its director has been receiving field-test data through a relay at Mercury.

nodes.t: Ships that work, not ships that look good
nodes.x: Colony One runs its diplomacy, military and trade through one directorate: resource flows, defence and the colony's strained dealings with everyone else. Miriam Vane resigns her US Navy commission to join it and helps design the Dustwing. In 2312 her son Silas takes a Dustwing, claims a war wreck in the Belt and in July turns its guns on the Americans. After the revolt it survives as a fleet with no state, keeping hidden anchorages alive.

nodes.t: Colony One's memory, and its spies
nodes.x: Ramón Ortiz kept an archive of every Earth order the colony was made to follow. It became Colony One's first intelligence office, and the office became a directorate: espionage, forecasting, counter-intelligence, applied research. In 2312 its analysts break the MRD's traffic on the Minangkabau mission while Torin Calder's black-ops team works in the field. After the revolt it carries on, keeping the record of the old war and the methods that went with it.

nodes.t: Repair sheds that became a maker
nodes.x: Begins as Colony One's repair sheds, keeping Washington's Teamster-S frames running long after Washington stops sending spares. By the 2250s a Dust Teamster has almost nothing American left in it, and by 2312 the sheds build the Ironback, Colony One's first frame of its own. After the revolt the works move into the hidden docks.

nodes.t: Research, espionage and trade under one roof
nodes.x: The MRD keeps its research, espionage and trade in a single bureau, alongside External and Defensive Affairs, which handles diplomacy and the military. Every programme goes before a panel, under the charter Lene Halden wrote. In 2312 Ana Lubov's bureau rewrites the inherited Union hulls' software to MRD standards, and Victor Blackhawk's intelligence service buys Project Hasta from a captain Colony One left without a ship.

nodes.t: Every drawing published
nodes.x: The MRD's frame works at Vesta. It began by refitting the Union's Pavise-S and Spiegel coilgun, and published every change for the panels, including the ones that turned out to make things worse. Its first frame of its own is built around Ana Lubov's metallic-hydrogen cell. In 2327 it is testing a catalysed fusion cell that walks for minutes at a time.

nodes.t: Lawful, commercial and American
nodes.x: The Constitutionalists govern through a Civic Government and deal with Earth's companies through the Corporate Liaison Office. Both were built out of the wreckage of the First Martian Crisis, with the stated purpose of ensuring that no Martian client state could again drag the United States into a colonial rebellion. They speak, and mean, the language of rights and contracts.

nodes.t: American drawings, Washington's lock
nodes.x: The Constitutionalists' arsenal builds American designs under the charter, each fitted with a deployment lock that only Washington can release, which the arsenal regards as a safeguard rather than a restriction. The Charter frame, the Charter Rifle and the Charter Carrier all come off its lines, and their crews take a certain pride in carrying the most lawful weapons on Mars.

nodes.t: Troubleshooters, not soldiers
nodes.x: The Syndicate doesn't govern; it trades. The Celestial Concord speaks for the clans in diplomacy, trade and research, with negotiators chosen by reputation, and Voidborne Security handles espionage and the military: pirate-hunters, clan enforcers, information-gatherers and, when the books call for it, reputation restorers. Jay Albedo is one of its best covert assets.

nodes.t: Crews that never sleep
nodes.x: Jay Albedo's enhancement business on Ceres. In 2312 it puts VIGOR on the market, a neural mesh and a weekly cobalt-blue pill that let a crew go without sleep, which by the houses' arithmetic works out cheaper than a second shift. The Ledger Conclave fills with MAC crews, the machine men. The name runs back to Dana Albedo, one of Vireo Cognition's first engineers.

nodes.t: Every tonne on the books
nodes.x: The houses' frame works at Pallas. It builds its first frames on Ascension's old Rigger, worker frames with a counting rig in the cab, because a house frame records every tonne it moves. It sells cheap drones to anyone with lithium to pay in, and after 2312 it builds the guard frames for the Great Exchange.

nodes.t: The thread between the tribes
nodes.x: Councils of genetic, ecological and life-systems specialists that began as stewards of communal resilience on Ganymede, and lost the Ganymede Split to the Lodges. They no longer govern Umoja. They run through it instead: a series of councils that every tribe sends someone to and none fully obeys, which decide how Umoja's people are cultivated and altered, keep the vats, and keep the keepers' word. Jupiter's radiation and cold made them paternalistic, though they still describe what they do as guardianship.

nodes.t: Frames that are grown
nodes.x: Umoja's works, where muscle is grown in vats and fitted to salvaged frames, and tended there like any other living thing. First came the Kinsman, then the Kith, the first frame Umoja grew from the start, and then the Kindred, lined with mats that eat Jupiter's radiation. Its transports are fed rather than fuelled.

nodes.t: Sworn pairs, Mitsurugi edges
nodes.x: It began by rebuilding the Nashik pilots' paired frames at Europa, with the Mitsurugi exiles' actuators and ice-water fuel cells. Its first original frame, the Nakula, rides out to hunt in Jupiter's radiation belts. Its Garuda, in 2327, runs on a frame fusion core of its own, and the works are further along than Beijing's analysts think.

nodes.t: Warrior cults that command what they grow
nodes.x: Umoja's warrior cults, descended from the raid cadres the Commonwealth caught at Ras Hafun and the grafted who followed them. Each Lodge is a war band, a family and a vat line at once, and since the Ganymede Split the Lodges have led Umoja. They command what they grow, hunt the Ashva's sworn pairs between trades, and recruit from the strays. Khalid Osman's name is still read at their musters.

nodes.t: A council that argues and never rules
nodes.x: The Compact's assembly, named for the town assemblies of old Novgorod that told princes what they could and couldn't do. Lev Arsenyev's Primorye crews brought the idea up with them. Every settlement and every akhara sends voices, and anyone may speak. It votes by acclamation, enforces nothing and holds no trials: disputes go to the akharas, to honour or to a fight. It is where Rahim Qureshi asked what the Compact would do if Moscow ever tried, and where it answered the Reclamation Bills with one word.

nodes.t: Warrior orders, not courts
nodes.x: The Compact's warrior orders, named for India's martial ascetic orders. Each keeps its own reading of the Oath: that enhancement is equipment owed back to the order, that the changed owe their first duty to the unchanged, or simply that the strong ride out. Some swear their riders in pairs, after Kavya Deshmukh's Ashvins; many don't. None of them answers to a court, and when an akhara is wrong, the only thing that can tell it so is another akhara.

nodes.t: A century of repairs
nodes.x: The Communion's builders rebuild the same Polaris-S frames generation after generation, until an Ember is a Polaris-S with a century of repairs in it and a name painted on by every pilot who has flown it. Their first new frame in a century, the Vigil, is built to sleep for years in the cold and wake ready.

nodes.t: Where American seals come off
nodes.x: The Mandate's seals hold only inside lunar orbit, so after the war Washington builds the nearest anchorage outside it: a dock at the Sun–Earth L2 point, four times the Moon's distance from Earth and a day's run from Hampton Roads. Carriers leave the L1 yard with the UNEL's seals fitted and stop at the Far Roads on the way out, where American engineers take the seals off and the plants run at whatever rating the Navy wants. The anchorage is American-led and open to allied hulls: Colony One's refit there before 2312, the Constitutionalists' after it. On the way home every ship stops again to be sealed.

nodes.t: A small anchorage in a lot of sunlight
nodes.x: The Ascendancy's main anchorage beyond the Moon is the joint one at Europa, months away. Its small one is Mercury: a dock in a polar crater in permanent shadow, beside the most sunlight in the system, where its breeders can be refitted with nobody watching and Burya-K frames stand guard. No one else has much use for Mercury, which suits the Ascendancy well enough. Moscow maintains that the abandoned Indian station in high orbit was never part of the dock.

nodes.t: The Commonwealth's door to the inner system
nodes.x: The Commonwealth's main anchorage beyond the Moon is the joint one at Europa, which it shares with the Ascendancy. In the inner system it has Eros, a near-Earth asteroid with a small dock where its frigates refit unsealed and its relief convoys stage on their way out. Eros is one of the Commonwealth's few holdings this side of Jupiter, which is why, when the Union surrounds it in 2312, the Commonwealth sends a battlegroup.

nodes.t: America's second anchorage, run by its colony
nodes.x: The yard on Phobos refits American hulls for Mars and builds Colony One's own; the first Dustwings come from its frames. Its staff are mostly American. Its authorities answer to Colony One. It is the US Navy's second anchorage beyond the Moon, where ships bound for Mars and Jupiter refit without going back to the Far Roads, and for three generations that gives the colony a hand on Washington's ships. In July 2312 the Rapid Defence Force takes the Forgeworks with one shot fired, and Washington runs it from then on.

nodes.t: Somewhere to dock
nodes.x: Before 2312 the Union refits its ships beyond the Moon at berths it keeps on Deimos, beside the array it built with the Directorate and on the Directorate's ground. In 2312 it tries to take Deimos outright, fails, and takes the Mars Trojans in a day instead. Those become its anchorage: captured rocks held by Hanse anchorage ships, with docks, air plants and garrisons, where Union hulls refit unsealed. Since then the Union has needed no colony of its own beyond the Moon.

nodes.t: The dragon keeps one dock
nodes.x: From the Juno Concession onwards, China's posts at Juno and Pallas are where its warships refit beyond the Moon, out of the UNEL's sight. When Beijing hands the posts to the Syndicate in 2312 it keeps one berth at Juno for its own ships, in a clause of the handover the houses were too pleased to read closely. Chinese hulls still refit there unsealed, inside the Syndicate's own exchange, beside the watchware China left behind.

EUX: Eurasian Pact · claimed by both halves

MINOR.t: Pirate crews take three tankers in a month
MINOR.x: Pirate crews seized three tankers in the strait in a single month. US carriers and Pact landing ships both arrived to escort shipping, and neither navy has fully left since. Japan, rather than send ships of its own, paid for a regional coast guard, which was the first time it had chosen to buy calm instead of fighting for it.

at: Salt flats of Bolivia, Chile and Argentina
MINOR.t: Two blocs bid for the battery metal
MINOR.x: The United States and the Union bid against each other for the salt flats' lithium. A coup attempt in Bolivia failed within days, and neither bloc ever admitted a role. Halcyon's whole battery bet rests on the supply contracts signed that winter. Brazil watched two blocs treat the continent as a quarry, and began looking across the Atlantic for partners who wouldn't.

MINOR.t: Mining walkers armoured against convoy raids
MINOR.x: Mining companies bolted steel plate onto legged construction walkers and used them to escort copper convoys through militia country. They were the first improvised mechs outside any bloc army. Brannock-Hale's lawyers tried to stop the walker sales and failed.

MINOR.t: US frames lent to a jungle counter-insurgency
MINOR.x: The United States lent two Garrison platoons to a Philippine counter-insurgency. Within a week the frames were mired to the knees, and insurgents with shoulder-fired rockets wrecked three of them. The Army quietly concluded that the Garrison was a frame for deserts and plains.

MINOR.t: A Tieniu crew walks its frame across the line
MINOR.x: A North Korean crew walked their export Tieniu across the DMZ and surrendered. Seoul handed it to the United States, whose engineers found the Iron Ox cruder than they had assumed and far harder to break.

MINOR.t: Turkey refuses frames on deck
MINOR.x: As the Pact built up forces for the Caspian, it asked to bring frame-carrying landing ships from its Baltic and Pacific fleets through the Bosporus and up the Volga–Don canal. Turkey refused anything with a mech on deck. The Pact fought the Caspian Crisis with the few landers already on the Caspian, and began building ground-effect craft there, which is why the Kaspiy exists.

MINOR.t: The first job for the firm that became Grey Lantern
MINOR.x: A mining consortium hired a small security firm whose four pilots had flown Garrisons for the US Army. They held a tin mine for eight months against three different militias and were paid in ore. The firm renamed itself Grey Lantern the following year.

MINOR.t: Export Tieshans guard a Pact-funded dam
MINOR.x: Tianlong engineering crews building a Pact-funded dam were guarded by export Tieshans, and downstream farmers blocked the river road for a month. No shots were fired, though every government in the region took note of whose frames were standing on the dam. That winter one company of the guards went unpaid and walked off into the Shan Hills, frames and all.

MINOR.t: Illegal logging crews fielding stolen walkers
MINOR.x: Illegal logging crews fielded stolen construction walkers and smuggled Tieniu under the canopy. Brazil bought a squadron of surplus Union Écuyers, whose quiet fuel cells and sensor heads found frames that helicopters flew straight over. Brasília has bought from Europe ever since, and increasingly sells to Africa.

MINOR.t: A rebel truce so the rescue frames can dig
MINOR.x: After a magnitude 8 earthquake, Japan sent Kizuna rescue frames by sea under the UN flag, and a UN envoy talked the government and a local insurgency into a truce so they could work. It held for ninety days, longer than either side expected.

MINOR.t: Tieshan-Kai frames set down on a disputed reef
MINOR.x: Tianshu chose the reef, and a Kaspiy-II landed a company of Tieshan-Kai on it. Philippine and Vietnamese patrol boats circled, and a Kestrel flight from a passing US carrier flew low overhead, but no one opened fire, and the frames are there still.

MINOR.t: Black-market Haboobs against Lantern Customs
MINOR.x: Insurgents with Haboobs bought on the League black market fought for the gas fields against a government that had hired Grey Lantern. The Lantern Customs won most engagements and the insurgents won the war of attrition, and by the end of it the gas companies had already pulled out.

MINOR.t: Three weeks, second-hand frames on both sides
MINOR.x: A three-week border war fought entirely with second-hand frames: Bolivia's Pact-supplied Tieshans against Paraguay's rebuilt ex-US Garrisons. The Tieshans won on the open scrub and lost in the river marshes. Arms dealers from four blocs attended the ceasefire talks. Brazil hosted them, and seated a League delegation at the table: the first time an African bloc helped end a South American war. For a year afterwards, a white squad walked the ceasefire line through the marshes: the first UN frames either army trusted to watch a border.

MINOR.t: Every container ship searched for frames
MINOR.x: After a ship later identified as a Lantern Tender transited the canal, Panama began opening containers on every vessel big enough to hide a frame. Every bloc has protested and every bloc has complied. Shipping times have doubled, and Washington's planners have started calling it the canal problem.

MINOR.t: Rescuers arrive to find the work already done
MINOR.x: When floods cut off Palu, Japanese rescue crews landed three days later to find the town's buried streets already dug out. Survivors described a giant that worked through the night and walked into the sea at dawn. Vireo's shell companies had bought industrial pumps in Makassar a week earlier.

MINOR.t: Mexico signs a defence and industry pact with Washington
MINOR.x: Mexico signed a defence and industry agreement with the United States: a Brannock-Hale frame line in Monterrey, swap pits along the Gulf coast, and a joint command for the northern border. Mexico City speaks of it as a partnership, while Washington's planning documents, which were not written for Mexican readers, list it under strategic depth.

MINOR.t: The Pact's own road to orbit
MINOR.x: A forty-kilometre magnetic track climbing the Tian Shan, built to throw hull sections into orbit so the Pact never has to depend on a lunar slipway. Tianlong laid the track and Tianshu times the launches; OKB-7 builds the sections. Its first launch went up this year. Both General Staffs claim the rail, and it sits where their railways meet.

MINOR.t: A sealed car that knocked
MINOR.x: A sealed rail car left Geneva for Marseille under Union military escort. Its manifest read 'laboratory equipment, 60 t'. Railway staff were told not to look inside, and reported that it knocked. It was loaded onto a ship registered to ████████ ████████ and sailed for ██████. Three weeks later the Union was fighting in the Great Sand Sea.

MINOR.t: Three satellites, one flash, nobody's test
MINOR.x: Three bloc satellites recorded a double flash over an atoll in the central Pacific. The signature fits neither a bomb nor a launch. The United States, which administers the atoll, called it a meteor. The Navy closed the sea around it for a month, and when the sea reopened, the atoll's airstrip was eight hundred metres longer.

MINOR.t: Britain's leased frames go home to America
MINOR.x: Britain leased forty Sparrowhawks from Halcyon in 2164, maintained by Halcyon crews at Lakenheath. A year later Washington recalled them for the Tiltrotor Drops in Iran. They came back in 2166 worn out, with an invoice for the wear. Britain paid it under the Burden Share and started asking Vauclair-Ehrlich about sensors.

MINOR.t: Iceland is told afterwards
MINOR.x: The US Air Force built a Kestrel swap pit at Keflavik to cover the Greenland–Iceland gap, under the Burden Share's basing clause, and told Iceland's government when the first battery crane was already standing. The Althing passed a protest unanimously. Washington replied that the pit protected Iceland too, and billed it for the runway.

MINOR.t: Quebec stops selling south at Washington's price
MINOR.x: Quebec's hydrogen had gone south for twenty years at the price the Burden Share set. In 2176 a Montreal consortium signed a contract to supply the Union's fuel-cell depots at three times that price, and Ottawa let it stand. Washington lodged a protest that it breached the compact, which Ottawa answered by describing the arrangement as a market. The Union's BZ-4 stacks have run partly on Quebec hydrogen ever since - and the provinces that profited are the ones that vote for the Halifax Motion.

MINOR.t: Norway is billed for Svalbard
MINOR.x: A year after Svalbard, where the United States and the Union fought over Norway's own archipelago, Washington sent Oslo its share of the Harrier refit as a Burden Share cost of defending Norwegian waters. Norway paid. Its parliament also voted to buy its next frames from Boreal and its sensors from the Union, and to send an observer to Strasbourg.

MINOR.t: Water for Mexico, a parts plant for Brannock-Hale
MINOR.x: After the third drought year on the border, Washington offered Mexico a real share of the Colorado and the Rio Bravo, and a seat on the river commission, in return for joint border patrols and a Brannock-Hale parts plant in Coahuila. It was the first agreement in a century that newspapers on both sides called fair. Washington, it turned out, would treat a neighbour it wanted to keep better than allies it took for granted, and that goodwill is why the Monterrey Accords take a week rather than a decade.

MAPNOTE: Three blocs and a neutral Japan

Before mechs. The United States, the Continental Union and the Eurasian Pact already face each other, and Japan stays out. Resource states across the Middle East, Africa and South Asia sign the Non-Aligned Declaration in 2159, three years after the Ares crew comes home from Mars. All of them share a biosphere already badly damaged by two centuries of warming, drowned coasts and failing harvests, and none of them is doing much about it. The United Nations, which moved to Geneva when New York's flood barriers failed, keeps count, and three bloc vetoes stop it doing anything else.
Mechs go to war in other people's countries

Iron Gate in the Zagros, the Pamir clash in the Wakhan Corridor, the Caspian Crisis over Azerbaijan, and an undeclared US–Union war over the Union's North African partners. Raiders from the Horn cross the Arabian Sea to a coast India can't defend. In orbit, station workers arm their Lifters.
The forty-minute war and the League

The Zarqa Campaign sets every bloc's doctrine. Convoy raids drive the blocs out of Africa and Arabia, leaving only the UN's white-painted escort frames, and in 2177 the African states found the Pan-African League on armed neutrality. The Pact digs in behind its fortress belt, and Japan fights its first mech action in the Yaeyama Islands.
Allies on paper, proxies in the sand

The two Western blocs fight at Svalbard. The Pact pushes into western Afghanistan, and India joins it. The League's civil war becomes three proxy wars in the Great Sand Sea, where Halden's H-17 is lost. In orbit, the first combat deaths, and on the Moon, Ascension's lunar half and the cities around its yard declare a republic, and the blocs carve up what is left of Ascension.
Deterrence by giants, and a home on Mars

Colony One is founded on Mars: the first permanent settlement on another planet. Above Earth, every bloc's first warships come off the Lunar Republic's slipway while each bloc builds its own way up, and the Republic's domes slide into a cold war over what Luna owes the planet below. On Earth, the Concord reveal sets off a public arms race and Moscow stockpiles siege weapons. In the Shan Hills, UN frames destroy a warlord nobody else was allowed to touch, and in Geneva the Secretary-General asks for a standing force and is vetoed three times. Meanwhile two supers that answer to no government protect civilians in the Great Sand Sea and at Herat. Underneath, the Pact splits in two behind a General Staff that now exists only on paper, Canada looks toward the Union, Mexico signs on with Washington, the League signs a defence charter in Khartoum while the Union's council deadlocks over it, and Mitsurugi starts copying its archives abroad.

The Third World War. Its major fronts run through Canada, South America, Europe, Central Asia, North Africa, the Middle East, Oceania and Alaska, and for the first time through orbit. The UN can't stop it, but holds open cities and refugee roads through it, and it ends when Luna's fleets force the peace under the UN's flag. The map shows where its fronts ran, and the five Earth powers that came out of it. Hatched states are front lines; pale fills mark influence without control.
The long rebuild

After the war ends, c. 2190, Earth is slowly helped back to its feet by the settlements it once fought over. The UNEL keeps the peace on Earth and Luna and locks away the war's worst weapons. Mars settles along a line between Colony One in the north and the Martian Research Directorate in the south, with independent colonies between them. The Syndicate's caravans carry the Belt's trade, pirates work the lanes beyond the patrols, and the earliest leavers' settlements at Pluto and Jupiter grow out of sight.
The First Martian Crisis

Eight months in 2312. The United States annexes Bolivia, a bioweapon kills an independent Martian colony, and the investigation into it finds a UNEL scientist receiving test data from Mercury. Every Earth power parks a battlegroup over Mars. In July Colony One turns on the United States, the MRD strikes Colony One from behind, the Union takes the Mars Trojans and the United States takes Phobos. On Earth nobody fires a shot: the war stays beyond Luna.
After Mars

The partisan war on Mars burns for years. Colony One's fleet escapes into the Belt, and the United States finishes what is left on the surface, keeps the ruined First City as a bastion and builds the Constitutionalists to replace the colony that turned on it. The MRD holds two thirds of the planet. In Geneva and on Luna, the UNEL's Earth First and Humanity First wings stop pretending to agree.
The Greater Solar Crisis
Projected. The setting of No Peace Past Luna, fifteen years after Mars. The faction summaries on the opening screen describe the powers and factions as they stand in 2327.

factions.n: United Nations of Earth and Luna
factions.h: United Nations and the Lunar Republic

POWERS.id: The richest power on Earth, and the one most willing to use its money and its armies to keep Earth in charge of what happens in space.
POWERS.seed: In the 2160s the United States led one of the three great blocs that divided the world. When frames changed warfare, it handed their design and building to two private companies, and those companies have worked hand in glove with the government ever since. It bars genetically or surgically altered people from military service, and treats keeping its soldiers unaltered as a point of national pride. In the Third World War it absorbed Mexico and took Central America, renaming itself the United States of the Americas, while European and Canadian allies who had spent decades paying for its protection went their own way. Just before the war it founded the first colony on Mars, and in the century after it crushed that colony when it rebelled and built a more obedient one to replace it.

POWERS.home: Strasbourg, where its nations meet · Paris, Berlin, London, Rome, Madrid, Warsaw
POWERS.id: A concert of European and North Atlantic nations, open to anyone of any colour who can join their elites: aristocratic, ceremonious, ascendant after Mars, and always competing over who leads.
POWERS.seed: Before the war, Europe's Continental Union could never act in time: every decision needed all of its members, and its forces were national contingents, each waiting on its own parliament. When the Russian siege armies rolled west the council stopped meeting, the Americans landed in Ireland and Spain, African interventions crossed into the south, and the nations held Berlin between themselves. What they rebuilt, joined by Britain, Iceland, Norway and eastern Canada, is the Transatlantic Union: a concert of national elites in which no member can stall the whole because none is allowed to lead it, and a mixing policy that places children of every origin in the nations' schools so that no city splits along old lines again. Those who won't choose a nation are dealt with quickly. The ethics panel's work went to Mars with the Union's old research station, which grew into one of the two great powers there; the Union keeps the conditions and has dropped the hearings. After 2312 it holds the Mars Trojans, and for a generation it is the strongest power beyond Luna.

POWERS.faith: Confucian order and AI-guided moral doctrine
POWERS.id: A disciplined technological state, run in close partnership with an artificial intelligence that plans its economy, its logistics and its wars.
POWERS.seed: China began the period as one half of the Eurasian Pact, an alliance with Russia, and later India. Its strength was mass production: simple, tough frames built in their thousands. Alongside them it grew Tianshu, a planning network that started out scheduling freight trains and ended up drafting every military plan for human officers to approve. China welcomes implants, network links and machine judgement, but refuses to alter the human body itself, and its quarrel with Moscow over exactly that split the Pact and became a civil war within the Third World War. Japan fell into China's sphere during the war. Afterwards China became patron to the merchant clans of the asteroid belt, and it remains one of Earth's five great powers.

POWERS.faith: Orthodox and Hindu traditions, no single creed
POWERS.id: Russia and India together: a hard-headed power that has promised never again to spend its own people's lives cheaply.
POWERS.seed: Both countries remember being used up. Russia remembers wars that cost a generation of young men, and India remembers decades of being out-built and out-armed by China. Inside the old Eurasian Pact, Moscow ran a secret programme, Department Zero, that turned pilots into components of their machines, and when Beijing demanded it be shut down, the Pact split. Russia and India fought China in the Third World War and came out of it as the Eurasian Ascendancy. The new state closed Department Zero and kept instead an oath its own Indian pilots had written: augmented soldiers are people the state owes, not parts it can use up. Those pilots it sent off-world with its blessing, and they became the Ashva Compact. The Ascendancy will do hard things when its people's survival demands it, and some inside its ministries would go further.

POWERS.faith: Plural and culturally powerful; no faith rules
POWERS.id: A union of African states that puts protecting people ahead of holding territory, and spreads its influence by selling and sheltering rather than occupying.
POWERS.seed: In the 2170s, after years of serving as the great blocs' battleground, Africa's resource states banded together as the Pan-African League and refused to take sides. A few years later they signed a charter in Khartoum promising to protect people before territory, and North African states from Morocco to Tunisia joined, bringing French and Italian engineering with them. The League fought the Third World War as the African Union, sheltering refugees from Europe and the Americas along the way, and came out of it as the African Commonwealth: plural, wary of empire, and an exporter of tough, cheap war machines to half the world. Its first act as a confident state was to send the raiders it had once fought beside, and the altered soldiers who chose to follow them, off the planet to Jupiter, where they founded Umoja.

HEIRS: Mexico joins and Western Canada stays. Eastern Canada, the United Kingdom, Iceland and Norway, billed for thirty years under the Burden Share, go over to the Union. Central America is taken in the war.
Too divided to act when the war comes. Its nations hold Berlin without it and refound it as a concert of their own elites, with Eastern Canada and the North Atlantic. Its Maghreb partners go south.
Takes in India, then splits: Beijing on one side, Moscow and Delhi on the other. Central Asia is the front.
Falls into China's sphere. Part of Mitsurugi escapes to Russia and the United States.
Becomes the African Union in the war and the Commonwealth after it. Its Gulf, Pakistani and Bangladeshi associates become a contested frontline.
United Nations of Earth and Luna

Ascension's lunar half, grown into the most advanced manufacturer off Earth. Builds every bloc's first warships and gives its best frames to the UN, hardens through a cold war in its own domes, and ends the war by putting its fleets under the UN, becoming UNEL's lunar half.
United Nations of Earth and Luna
Vetoed for fifty years, ignored through the war, and handed a navy at the end of it. Its relief agencies and white squads become UNEL's two halves.

UNEL.n: United Nations of Earth and Luna
UNEL.home: Geneva and the Luna Custodian Bastion
UNEL.id: The institution that ended the Third World War, and has kept the peace on Earth and the Moon ever since, with its own navy and a mandate to protect humanity from itself.
UNEL.seed: Two things came together to make it. One was the old United Nations, moved to Geneva after New York flooded and blocked for decades by the great powers' vetoes, which kept working anyway: escorting food convoys, guarding refugee camps and fielding peacekeepers in borrowed frames painted white. The other was the Lunar Republic, a state formed by the engineers and families who ran the shipyards on the Moon, where every power's first warships were built. When the war turned atomic, the Republic refused to build for anyone, handed its fleets to the UN and closed the routes down to Earth until the fighting stopped. The United Nations of Earth and Luna that resulted controls which reactors may come near Earth, and the beamed power that runs much of the reconstruction. A century on, it is split between those who think it exists to protect Earth from its colonies and those who think it should protect people wherever they live.

SPACE.home: The First City, now the US-held Colony One Bastion · dispersed
SPACE.faith: A civic religion of Martian survival
SPACE.id: What remains of humanity's first settlement on Mars: founded by the United States, crushed by it when it rebelled, and now a hidden fleet and an underground network.
SPACE.seed: Colony One was founded in 2186, just before the Third World War, as the first permanent human home on another planet. Its settlers were chosen for one thing, whether they could keep themselves alive without help, and took the radiation-hardening gene treatment Mars demands, even though it barred them from American government service. They grew up in the war's wreckage, governed from Washington by a charter they resented and by orders that arrived months late. For more than a century they held the north of Mars against a rival state in the south. In 2312 they finally turned on the United States, and lost. What survives is a fleet hiding in the asteroid belt and a resistance network on Mars, both still committed to the idea that Mars should answer to no one.

SPACE.faith: Free, with a Catholic plurality and a civic faith in the charter
SPACE.id: The law-abiding American state on Mars, built after Colony One's revolt so that no Martian colony could ever again drag Washington into a war.
SPACE.seed: Its roots go back to 2186, when a group of American legislators wrote a charter for future American territory in space: rights for every settler, genetically altered or not, and the power to make war kept firmly in Washington. Washington shelved it. Around the same time, Mexican water engineers and judges joined the young colony on Mars, bringing a tradition of settling disputes over water by law rather than by force. When Colony One rebelled in 2312, those river families refused to join the revolt and kept the water flowing to both sides. Afterwards the old charter was taken out of storage and ratified at a new capital, New Philadelphia. The Constitutionalists now hold a third of Mars, and none of their weapons can be used without a code from Washington.

SPACE.id: A scientific, carefully governed state that holds two thirds of Mars and allows human enhancement only where it can be shown to be necessary.
SPACE.seed: It began as a European research station on Mars, staffed by scientists disgraced after their Geneva institute grew a giant war organism that went badly wrong. Europe's answer to that scandal was an ethics panel with the power to stop any programme, and four hundred pages of conditions. During the Third World War the Union ordered the station to grow enhanced soldiers for the European front. The station refused, citing the panel's own rules, and the panel backed it against the government that had created it. Those rules became the founding charter of the Martian Research Directorate. It holds the south of Mars, publishes its research, rations its use of force, and in 2312 broke Colony One with a cyberweapon and a strike from behind.

SPACE.id: A wandering merchant power in the asteroid belt, organised through markets, contracts and caravans rather than territory, with China as its patron.
SPACE.seed: Its founders were Chinese prospecting families sent out to survey asteroids, who were so far from home that they began keeping their own accounts, trading among themselves and settling disputes by reputation. They called themselves houses. Rather than rein them in, Beijing chartered them under a grand name a government clerk chose, the Celestial Prosperity Syndicate, and during the war it leased them its ships in the belt rather than lose the belt altogether. The lease was never ended. Today the Syndicate's caravans are fleets and markets at once, it runs the belt's great exchanges, and it is rich enough to think it no longer needs Beijing, which keeps watch all the same.

SPACE.id: A society of genetically and surgically altered people on Jupiter's moons, held together by kinship and an ethic of caring for what they grow, and led by warrior lodges.
SPACE.seed: For decades before the war, Earth argued over who might change a human body and who could license it. Low-gravity workers, back-street clinics and raiders were all altered in their own ways, and in 2183 forty thousand altered people walked to Geneva to ask for one licence that every government would honour. They called themselves Umoja, Swahili for unity, and were refused. In the war, African field hospitals learned to graft living tissue that kept soldiers alive through wounds that should have killed them. When it ended, the African Commonwealth sent the raiders and grafted soldiers off the planet rather than deal with them at home, and they went to Jupiter. There, on Ganymede, they split between those who believed that what is grown must be cared for and those who believed it can be commanded, and the commanders won. Altered people across the solar system still lean towards Umoja, more than will admit it.

SPACE.id: An honour-bound society on Jupiter's moons Europa and Io, built around sworn pairs of warriors and one conviction: the strong must defend the weak.
SPACE.seed: Before the war, Indian pilots augmented to fly Russia's best frames refused to be handed over to a secret programme that treated pilots as parts. Instead they wrote an oath whose root is that the strong defend the weak. Russian shipyard workers from the Far East, altered for work in orbit and then refused licences at home, hid the pilots at Vladivostok, along with Japanese engineers who had fled when Japan fell under China's influence. When the war ended, Russia and India gave them a ship and sent them away with a blessing rather than try to control them. They settled Europa and Io as the Ashva Compact, alongside Russian and Indian settlements that never recognised them, with warrior orders instead of courts and an assembly that argues but never rules. A century later the Eurasian Ascendancy wants back what it gave.

SPACE.faith: Theocratic: a faith of the distant sun
SPACE.id: A remote religious civilisation in the far outer solar system, whose people worship a sun they can barely see.
SPACE.seed: Its people descend from refugees of the Third World War who fled to the Arctic and Antarctic ice, where no army wanted to follow, and learned to live on almost no heat, power or outside help. In time they carried those habits into deep space, following the handful of settlers who had left before the war and gone as far as Pluto. Out there, in the cold and the dark, a faith grew: a patient, communal worship of the distant sun. For a century the inner solar system lost track of them entirely. The faith came back in 2312 aboard an old warship from Pluto, and the merchant caravans of the asteroid belt, seeing a market, have been spreading it ever since.

TIMELINE.arc: An alliance leader that ends the period trusting its corporations more than its allies.
end: United States of the Americas

A corporate-backed hard power holding Mexico, Central America and Western Canada. It funds Colony One, crushes its rebellion, builds the Constitutionalists to replace it, and keeps the ruined First City as a US-held bastion.
ev: The richest bloc: armour holds, air power strikes deep.
Outbids the Union for South American lithium; Halcyon bets on batteries.
Iron Gate: four Garrisons win the first mech battle.
The Partnership Act hands frame procurement to Brannock-Hale and Halcyon.

Undeclared strikes ground the Union's fleet at its Maghreb depots.
Operation Highland breaks on the Fortress Belt.
Svalbard: a Union lance shoots Kestrels mid-transformation.
Harriers with point-defence lasers answer Svalbard and the Air Umbrella.
The Concord reveal starts a public super-robot arms race.
Unaltered Crews: biological purity becomes regulation.
Canada's Halifax Motion; Mexico signs the Monterrey Accords.
Mexico joins and Central America is taken: the United States of the Americas.
Canada splits; the west stays. South America becomes a front.
Oceania, then Alaska, and an atomic exchange that destroys Vancouver.

Britain's leased Sparrowhawks are recalled for the Tiltrotor Drops and come back worn out, with an invoice.
A Kestrel swap pit goes in at Keflavik, and Iceland is told afterwards.
Halcyon threatens Britain's Kestrel support over a Haubert licence.
Norway is billed for the Harrier refit after Svalbard.
The Rio Bravo compact: water for Mexico, a parts plant for Brannock-Hale.
Britain is refused a berth at Hampton Roads and asks Strasbourg instead.
The Loyal Minority: forty-one votes against Unaltered Crews, and a charter for Mars that Washington shelves.
Battery frames come back on lithium from space

TIMELINE.arc: Quality, ethics and a council that can never agree in time, until its nations stop waiting for it.
end: Transatlantic Union

Refounded in Strasbourg as a concert of national elites, with Eastern Canada and the North Atlantic. Its Mars programme becomes the Martian Research Directorate, which keeps the Union's conditions and not its orders, and after 2312 the Union is the strongest power beyond Luna.
ev: Licenses the Garrison as the Écuyer.
The Maghreb Depot Strikes: blinded and grounded in two weeks.
Directive 5: blind the enemy first, then fight.
Funds Halden's ███████ tissue programme in Geneva.
Opens a Haubert line in Tunis for its North African partners.
Svalbard: the hunter-killer lance and the Union's first famous ace.
Secretly sends Halden's H-17 into the Great Sand Sea, and loses it.
Directive 10: every programme goes before an ethics panel.
The Long Session: the council can't agree how to answer Khartoum.
Halden proposes a supervised research station on Mars.
Roland: the only super the ethics panel approves.
The European Front: the council is still voting as the line breaks.
American landings in Ireland and Spain; African landings in the south.
The Defence of Berlin: the nations hold the line the council couldn't.
Eastern Canada, the United Kingdom, Iceland and Norway come over.
The Battle of Yernon: one British dreadnought breaks the Russian inner fleet.

Refounded as a concert of national elites
Cyprus, and Tunis handed back on a lease

Holds anchorages of its own beyond Luna

end: Split, and sent north

The west stays with the United States and the east goes to the Transatlantic Union. The Winter War empties the towns along the line, and the camps its refugees build on the Arctic ice send people into the deep system.

After Svalbard, the Wolverine is built to be seen last.
The Aurora's pilots, one from Calgary and one from Montreal, start training together.
The Halifax Motion passes by eleven votes.

TIMELINE.arc: Mass production, then a network that plans the wars.
end: China

Tianshu begins as the scheduler for the frame trains.

The Air Umbrella, cued by Tianshu.

TIMELINE.arc: Quality, augmentation and siege trains, and a partner that joins because it is tired of losing.
end: Eurasian Ascendancy

Russia and India, determined that their people will never again be spent. Department Zero is closed and the Nashik Oath kept. The Nashik pilots and Mitsurugi's exiles are sent off with its blessing, and become the Ashva Compact.
ev: OKB-7 builds interceptors and bombers for deep-battle doctrine.
Turkey closes the Bosporus to frames; the Pact starts building ground-effect craft on the Caspian.
The Caspian Crisis: loses at Talysh, but steals the LR-1.
The Medved: the Pact's first frame built for quality over numbers.
The Hari River Offensive; the augmented Volk is first seen.
The Delhi Accession: India joins, and OKB-7 opens a line at Nashik.
Koschei: the pilot becomes the control system.
The Siege Question: Tsars and a 50 m shape on the flatcars.

The Nashik Oath: augmented, but never consumed.
Morevna: a Koschei pilot walks off the range.
The Staya: six Volks sent to bring Morevna back.
The Pact Civil War, then the siege trains turn west into Europe.
Across the Bering Strait into Alaska.

Delhi buys export Tieshans from Beijing, and waits on Tianshu for spares.

The Hegemony keeps Department Zero's arithmetic
Destroys its own station at Mercury
The Reclamation Bills ask the Ashva to come back

TIMELINE.arc: Neutral because everyone needs its parts, until someone wants the factory.
end: China's sphere
Japan is absorbed. The Mitsurugi engineers who left through Vladivostok carry their actuators toward the Ashva Compact.
ev: Defensive by law, and rich from exports.
After the Malacca seizures, pays for a coast guard instead of fighting.
The Japanese public meets mechs as rescuers: the Kizuna.
The Yaeyama Incidents: Hayates' first combat, against frames nobody claims.
Licence Diplomacy: sell critical parts to everyone.
Kizuna frames dig out Aceh under a rebel truce.
An infiltration team goes for the Raijin; the one captured is Grey Lantern.
Takemikazuchi: a fusion reactor that only a shrine-trained pilot can steady.
The Osaka dispute; Mitsurugi registers subsidiaries in Vladivostok and Ohio.
Someone takes the factory, and Japan falls into China's sphere.
Grain credits from Beijing, and Tianshu starts scheduling Japan's ports.
The Kansai Coalition wins the Diet on a promise to settle with Beijing.
Osaka's capacitors go into the fusion torch
The Kizuna lullaby, sung at every protest
